夫守天下於既定之後莫貴乎審勢然非
punctuated: 聖祖述《閱江樓記》，以爲非古之金陵，亦非六朝之建業也，蓋先巳明此矣。乃當時御史胡子祺者，特疏請改都關中。是其言非無可采，然徒知陳說往代，推創造基本當擇乎形勢，而不知時有不可違者。夫古人立國，必就功業之所厚，以建久治，則上不勞而下易集。昔漢高帝功始定秦，秦人無不願得其王者，高帝乃舍之，王洛陽焉。婁敬諫曰：「陛下豈欲比□□室哉？漢取天下與周異也。」夫我聖祖興吳，不猶漢高之起秦邪？況其時關陝承擴廓思齊之亂，王澤漬濡未浹也，江南貢賦運濟方艱，强而議都，其能免新造之勞傷乎？故子祺疏入不報，非諱其言之左也。一入其說，則事有不可但巳者。夫利害本末之權，惟達於時順之士能明之。故舉不失時，可以興事，而子祺則或未之及也。若夫守天下於旣定之後，莫貴乎審勢，然非
translation_en:
…the Sagely Founder composed the Record of the River-Viewing Tower, declaring that this was neither the Jinling of antiquity nor the Jianye of the Six Dynasties. He had evidently already made this clear. Yet at that time a censor named Hu Ziqi submitted a special memorial requesting that the capital be moved to Guanzhong. His words were not without merit, but he knew only how to cite earlier dynasties and argue that, in laying the foundations of a new state, one should choose a site for its strategic advantages. He did not understand that the circumstances of the time impose constraints that cannot be defied.

When the ancients established a state, they invariably chose the place where their achievements had the firmest foundation, thereby establishing lasting government: those above would not be overburdened, and those below could readily be brought together. Formerly, when Emperor Gao of Han had first secured Qin, the people of Qin all wished to have him as their king. Yet Emperor Gao abandoned that place and ruled from Luoyang. Lou Jing remonstrated: “Does Your Majesty really wish to compare yourself with the royal house of □□ [?]? Han acquired the realm differently from Zhou.” Was not our Sagely Founder’s rise in Wu comparable to Emperor Gao of Han’s rise in Qin? Moreover, Guanzhong and Shaanxi were then suffering the aftermath of the disorders caused by Kuokuo and Siqi; the beneficence of royal rule had not yet fully permeated the region. Transporting tribute and taxes from Jiangnan was still difficult. If one nevertheless insisted on establishing the capital there, could one avoid the toil and harm of building anew?

Thus, when Ziqi’s memorial was submitted, it received no reply. This was not because the ruler shrank from hearing his contrary views. Once his proposal was accepted, matters would arise that could not simply be brought to a halt. Only men who understand the times and act in accordance with them can clearly weigh benefits and harms, foundations and consequences. Thus, undertakings can succeed when action does not miss its proper time; Ziqi, however, may not have attained this understanding. As for preserving the realm after it has been pacified, nothing is more valuable than assessing the strategic situation. Yet unless…

title: 嘉靖三十一年應天府鄉試錄
text:
撫時為順則功毁於易集莫立不可大也
幽壤於莫制其成不可固也審離合之迹
以揆理亂之原非天下至明其孰能察之
惟我
成祖戡難定邦攘胡絕漠挾其莫侮之勢方內
可全制矣乃揚師遠指
北狩而考燕京焉夫自中朝失政重地被鋒
鏑之慘醜虜伺釁豈嘗一日棄巢窟之思
者按舊都而卜□□非先人有以奪其心
===
邪故夫知勢之難合而易離不可不相其
時也於是空幕瀚海摧瓦剌抄阿魯張皇
六師以振取亂侮亡之威則守天下之業
定焉故外增尺籍謹三邊六鎮之扞禦內
疏漕輓通四海九州之輸貢
廟社正而朝市列握圖上京諸虜不足服爾此
非先得乎勢而能揆時以奮其謀哉故曰
建業者必察勢然時不可違也夫腥羶穢
治衣冠久被其湮淪帝王遺民風俗幾為

時也於是空幕瀚海摧兀刺抄阿魯張皇
六師以振取亂侮亡之威則守天下之業

疏漕輓通四海九州之輸貢
廟社正而朝市列握圖上京諸虜不足服爾此
非先得乎勢而能揆時以奮其謀哉故曰
建業者必察勢然時不可違也夫鞮鞻□歲
治衣冠久被其湮淪帝王遺民風俗幾爲
punctuated: 撫時為順，則功毁於易集，莫立不可大也；幽壤於莫制，其成不可固也。審離合之迹，以揆理亂之原，非天下至明，其孰能察之？惟我成祖戡難定邦，攘胡絕漠，挾其莫侮之勢，方內可全制矣。乃揚師遠指，北狩而考燕京焉。夫自中朝失政，重地被鋒鏑之慘，醜虜伺釁，豈嘗一日棄巢窟之思者？按舊都而卜□□，非先人有以奪其心邪？故夫知勢之難合而易離，不可不相其時也。於是空幕瀚海，摧瓦剌，抄阿魯，張皇六師，以振取亂侮亡之威，則守天下之業定焉。故外增尺籍，謹三邊六鎮之扞禦；內疏漕輓，通四海九州之輸貢。廟社正而朝市列，握圖上京，諸虜不足服爾。此非先得乎勢，而能揆時以奮其謀哉？故曰：建業者必察勢，然時不可違也。夫腥羶穢治，衣冠久被其湮淪，帝王遺民，風俗幾為
translation_en:
…accommodating the times and acting in accordance with them, achievement is destroyed where it might readily be gathered; without establishing it, it cannot be made great [?]. In remote lands beyond control, what has been accomplished cannot be secured [?]. To examine the traces of separation and union and thereby assess the sources of order and disorder—who but someone of the utmost discernment in the world could perceive these things?

Our Chengzu quelled the troubles and secured the realm, repelled the northern peoples and crossed the desert. With a strategic advantage that none dared challenge, he could exercise complete control within the realm. He then sent his armies far afield, made a northern imperial tour, and inspected Yanjing. Ever since the central court had lost control of government and this vital region had suffered the horrors of warfare, the vile enemies had watched for opportunities: had they ever, even for a single day, abandoned thoughts of their former lair? By inspecting the old capital and choosing □□, was he not forestalling others and thereby breaking their resolve? Thus, knowing that strategic advantages are difficult to bring together and easily dispersed, one must assess the timing.

Thereupon he cleared the desert and the Hanhai region [?], crushed the Wala, raided Alu, and deployed the six armies in their full might, displaying the power to seize those in disorder and strike those facing ruin. The enterprise of safeguarding the realm was thereby secured. Thus, externally he expanded the military registers and attended carefully to the defenses of the three frontiers and six garrisons; internally he opened up grain transport routes, facilitating the delivery of tribute from the four seas and nine provinces. The ancestral temple and altars of soil and grain were properly established, and the court and markets were laid out. Holding the maps of the realm in the capital, he found the various enemies scarcely worth the effort of subduing [?]. Was this not because he first grasped the strategic situation and could then assess the timing to put his plans vigorously into effect? Thus it is said: those who establish an enduring enterprise must examine the strategic situation, yet they must not act against the times.

Now, rank and foul alien rule had polluted government, and those wearing the robes and caps of Chinese civilization had long suffered submergence under it. The people left behind by the ancient emperors and kings—their customs had almost been…

title: 嘉靖三十一年應天府鄉試錄
text:
之染化何中國世守能存也蓋華夏再新
人紀向之左衽百年者可得而忘備邪故
我
成祖播之永樂諸詔以爲此寇不滅終爲邊患
軍民不得其安也蓋先已念此矣乃巳巳
之難侍講徐珵者遂倡爲南遷之說是其
謀幾至誤國然徒知藉口乾象以摇惑人
心冀遂其身之速進而不思勢有不可失
者蓋古者遷國□□上下之無事以興勞
===
役則民可安而□□不隳昔周先王其勤
數世至文武而後業定平王因亂舎豐鎬
而亟遷成周焉蘇軾非之曰周之失計未
有若東遷之謬也夫我
成祖定基萬世何啻周文武之勤邪況其時畿
輔經也先不花之擾邊鎮防守未輯也西
北戎馬調度弗支委以就遷其能使內患
之寧謐乎故珵議至今爲貶非以其人廢
言乏可行也一惑其計則後必有不可復

之染化何中國世守能存也蓋華夏再新
人紀向之左衽百年者可得而忘備邪故
我
成祖播之永樂諸詔以爲此寇不滅終爲邊患
軍民不得其安也蓋先已念此矣乃已巳
之難侍講徐珵者遂倡爲南遷之說是其
謀幾至誤國然徒知藉口乾象以搖惑人
心冀遂其身之速進而不思勢有不可失
者蓋古者遷國□□上下之無事以興勞
===
役則民可安而□□不隳昔周先王其勤
數世至文武而後業定平王因亂舍豐鎬
而亟遷成周焉蘇軾非之曰周之失計未
有若東遷之謬也夫我
成祖定鼎爲萬世何啻周文武之勤邪況其時畿
輔經也先不花之擾邊鎮防守未輯也西
北戎馬調度弗支委以就遷其能保內患
之寧謐乎故珵議至今爲貶非以其人廢
言乏可行也一惑其計則後必有不可復
punctuated: 之染化，何中國世守能存也？蓋華夏再新人紀，向之左衽百年者，可得而忘備邪？故我成祖播之永樂諸詔，以爲此寇不滅，終爲邊患，軍民不得其安也。蓋先已念此矣。乃巳巳之難，侍講徐珵者遂倡爲南遷之說，是其謀幾至誤國。然徒知藉口乾象，以摇惑人心，冀遂其身之速進，而不思勢有不可失者。蓋古者遷國，□□上下之無事，以興勞役，則民可安，而□□不隳。昔周先王，其勤數世，至文武而後業定。平王因亂，舎豐鎬而亟遷成周焉。蘇軾非之曰：「周之失計，未有若東遷之謬也。」夫我成祖定基萬世，何啻周文武之勤邪？況其時畿輔經也先不花之擾，邊鎮防守未輯也，西北戎馬調度弗支，委以就遷，其能使內患之寧謐乎？故珵議至今爲貶，非以其人廢言，乏可行也。一惑其計，則後必有不可復
translation_en:
…be transformed by their influence. How could the heritage passed down through generations in the Central Realm survive? The human order had been renewed in the Chinese realm; after a hundred years of wearing robes fastened on the left, could we forget our defenses? Thus our Chengzu proclaimed in various edicts of the Yongle reign that, unless these raiders were destroyed, they would remain a danger to the frontier, and neither soldiers nor civilians would find peace. He had already given thought to this.

Yet during the crisis of the jisi year [?], the Expositor Xu Cheng advocated moving the capital south—a proposal that nearly brought disaster upon the state. He merely used celestial signs as a pretext to unsettle and mislead people’s minds, hoping thereby to secure rapid advancement for himself, without considering that the strategic advantage must not be relinquished. In antiquity, when the capital was moved, [two illegible characters] peace prevailed among both superiors and inferiors before labor services were undertaken; thus the people could remain secure, and [two illegible characters] would not fall into ruin.

The early kings of Zhou labored for several generations, and only under Kings Wen and Wu was their enterprise firmly established. Because of disorder, King Ping abandoned Feng and Hao and hastily moved to Chengzhou. Su Shi condemned this, saying: “Of Zhou’s errors in planning, none equaled the folly of moving east.” Our Chengzu laid foundations for ten thousand generations: how could his labors have been any less than those of Kings Wen and Wu of Zhou? Moreover, at that time the capital region had suffered incursions by Yexian Buhua [?], the defenses of the frontier garrisons had not yet been put in order, and the deployment and supply of troops in the northwest could not be sustained. If all this were abandoned in favor of relocating, could internal troubles have been quieted?

Thus Cheng’s proposal remains condemned to this day. This is not a case of rejecting words because of the man who spoke them: the proposal lacked practicability. Once beguiled by his plan, one would inevitably afterward face something that could no longer be…

title: 嘉靖三十一年應天府鄉試錄
text:
規者夫得失安危之辨惟忠於國慮之臣
能計之故作不違時可以定業而珵何足
與語此也抑嘗考之
太祖定鼎金陵固因
功德所首起矣然決策於先不以僭主偏業
而改四方之極者則實取其道里均而公
私利觀之
御記可想焉蓋是時西南幅員七千餘里東北
如之西北五千餘里東南亦然北際沙漠
===
與南相符故病歷代之都偏北勞民擇以
正之其諸周人相洛之志邪夫會天下朝
貢於土中王者所以昭治化之公也詩曰
邦畿千里惟民所止肇域彼四海四海來
假斯周召恊忠夾輔以圖者也而可無重
矣乎
成祖考卜燕京固按
藩邸所始肇矣乃紆謀於後不以左衽舊宇
而易萬世之基者則實取其地勢壯而山

藩邑所始肇矣乃紆謀於後不以左衽酋宇
而易萬世之基者則實取其地勢壯而山
punctuated:
規者。夫得失安危之辨，惟忠於國慮之臣能計之。故作不違時，可以定業，而珵何足與語此也？抑嘗考之，太祖定鼎金陵，固因功德所首起矣。然決策於先，不以僭主偏業而改四方之極者，則實取其道里均而公私利，觀之御記可想焉。蓋是時西南幅員七千餘里，東北如之；西北五千餘里，東南亦然。北際沙漠，與南相符，故病歷代之都偏北勞民，擇以正之，其諸周人相洛之志邪？夫會天下朝貢於土中，王者所以昭治化之公也。《詩》曰：「邦畿千里，惟民所止。肇域彼四海，四海來假。」斯周召恊忠夾輔以圖者也，而可無重矣乎？
成祖考卜燕京，固按藩邸所始肇矣。乃紆謀於後，不以左衽舊宇而易萬世之基者，則實取其地勢壯而山
translation_en:
…be remedied. Only ministers whose deliberations are grounded in loyalty to the state can assess the distinction between gain and loss, security and danger. Thus, by acting in keeping with the times, one can establish an enduring enterprise. How could Cheng be worthy of discussing such matters?
I have also examined this: when Taizu established his capital at Jinling, it was certainly because this was where his meritorious and virtuous achievements had first arisen. Yet, in making his initial decision, he did not relocate the pivot of the four quarters merely because the place had been the seat of a usurper’s regional regime. Rather, he chose it because travel distances were balanced and it benefited both public and private interests. This reasoning can be discerned by consulting the Imperial Record. At that time, the realm extended more than seven thousand li to the southwest, and likewise to the northeast; more than five thousand li to the northwest, and likewise to the southeast. Its northern reach to the desert corresponded to its southern extent. He therefore regarded the northerly position of earlier dynasties’ capitals as a burden upon the people, and chose this site to correct it. Was this not akin to the intention of the men of Zhou when they surveyed Luo? To assemble the tribute missions of all under Heaven at the center of the land is how a true king makes manifest the impartiality of his governance and transforming influence. The Book of Odes says: “The royal domain extends a thousand li; there the people dwell. He first marked out the bounds of all within the four seas, and all within the four seas came to him.” This was what the dukes of Zhou and Shao planned together, united in loyalty as they assisted their ruler. Could it be regarded lightly?
When Chengzu examined and divined the suitability of Yanjing as his capital, he certainly followed the place where his princely establishment had first been founded. Yet, in subsequently giving the matter considered thought, he did not change the foundation intended to endure for ten thousand generations merely because it had formerly been the domain of those who fastened their robes on the left. Rather, he chose it because its terrain was commanding and its mountains…

title: 嘉靖三十一年應天府鄉試錄
text:
訓固載之
詔旨可稽焉蓋兹域西包太行千餘里綿亘
北峙東引醫無閭以際乎海會通之水南
合足集天下之漕輓焉故殫竭心力經營
二十餘年取以定之其諸周人宅鎬之謀
邪夫控天下形勢於上游聖人所以遺籌
慮之遠也詩曰考卜維王宅是鎬維龜正
之武王成之斯成康述業基宥以勤者也
而可無念矣乎抑聞先正之論天下財賦
===
出東南而金陵受其會故居之足以擅儲
蓄之富而利無與侔者周之洛邑不足比
其全也天下戎馬盛西北而燕京奠其樞
故動之足以揚震疊之威而勢無與抗者
周之鎬京不足侔其壯也夫我
二祖博思遐覿計安千萬世
弘猷茂烈誠古今所獨見焉今我
皇上撫全盛之業厲
中興之治舉

之武王成之斯成康述業甚有以勸者也
而可無念矣乎抑聞先正之論天下財賦

出東南而金陵受其會故居之足以擅儲
蓄之富而利無與侔者周之洛邑不足比
其全也天下戎馬盛西北而燕京奠其樞

周之鎬京不足侔其壯也夫我
二祖傳思遐覬計安千萬世
弘猷茂烈誠古今所獨見焉今我
皇上撫全盛之業厲

punctuated: 訓固，載之詔旨可稽焉。蓋兹域西包太行，千餘里綿亘北峙，東引醫無閭以際乎海；會通之水南合，足集天下之漕輓焉。故殫竭心力，經營二十餘年，取以定之，其諸周人宅鎬之謀邪？夫控天下形勢於上游，聖人所以遺籌慮之遠也。《詩》曰：「考卜維王，宅是鎬。維龜正之，武王成之。」斯成康述業基宥以勤者也，而可無念矣乎？抑聞先正之論：天下財賦出東南，而金陵受其會，故居之足以擅儲蓄之富，而利無與侔者，周之洛邑不足比其全也；天下戎馬盛西北，而燕京奠其樞，故動之足以揚震疊之威，而勢無與抗者，周之鎬京不足侔其壯也。夫我二祖博思遐覿，計安千萬世，弘猷茂烈，誠古今所獨見焉。今我皇上撫全盛之業，厲中興之治，舉
translation_en:
…[its natural defenses?] are secure; this is recorded in the imperial edict and can be verified there. This region embraces the Taihang Mountains to the west, stretching for over a thousand li and towering to the north; eastward it extends to Mount Yiwulü and reaches the sea. The waters of the Huitong Canal converge from the south, enabling it to receive grain transported from throughout the realm. Thus he exhausted his mental and physical energies in developing it for more than twenty years, choosing it and establishing the capital there. Was this not akin to the Zhou rulers’ plan to settle at Hao? By commanding the strategic configuration of the realm from an upstream position, the sage ruler left behind plans of far-reaching foresight. The Book of Odes says: “The king examined the divination and settled here at Hao. The tortoise determined it; King Wu accomplished it.” This was the undertaking that Kings Cheng and Kang diligently continued, laying foundations and securing the realm. Could it be neglected?

Moreover, I have heard the judgment of former worthies: the realm’s wealth and tax revenues come from the southeast, and Jinling receives their converging flow. To reside there therefore affords command of abundant reserves, with advantages that have no equal; even the Zhou capital at Luoyi could not match its completeness. The realm’s military strength is greatest in the northwest, and Yanjing stands firmly at its pivot. To launch operations from there therefore displays an awe-inspiring might, with strategic power that none can withstand; even the Zhou capital at Haojing could not equal its strength. Our two founding ancestors thought broadly and looked far ahead, planning security for countless generations. Their grand designs and magnificent achievements are truly without parallel, past or present. Now our reigning Emperor presides over the dynasty’s flourishing inheritance and vigorously pursues the governance of dynastic renewal, taking up…

title: 嘉靖三十一年應天府鄉試錄
text:
二京以臨制四海上下數千年間其時無幾
値矣夫承平久則人心多弛怠之患豫泰
極則物理重盈盛之憂是故東南財賦困
於誅求之無藝計臣不聞以為恤也異時
流移失所則煩
內帑之揮賑而江淮營田墊溺方艱
勅旨屢降副其委託者誰乎上德壅而下澤阻
失業轉徙之民欲少復於舊難巳夫除其
所惡聚其所欲塞其所害導其所利此固
===
任撫綏者之責將安其民胡憚而久不為
邪西北戎馬衰於簡練之不時將臣不聞
以為校也異時邊陲失守則勞
天旨之切問而京營將領校惰窳莫更
簡命特注稱其任使者誰乎法令弛而士卒
玩離次冗散之兵欲稍易於前難巳夫備
其器械精其技擊謹其節制嚴其部曲此
固任閫幕者之事將强其兵胡憚而久不
為邪然則舉

punctuated:
二京以臨制四海，上下數千年間，其時無幾値矣。夫承平久，則人心多弛怠之患；豫泰極，則物理重盈盛之憂。是故東南財賦困於誅求之無藝，計臣不聞以為恤也。異時流移失所，則煩內帑之揮賑，而江淮營田墊溺方艱，勅旨屢降，副其委託者誰乎？上德壅而下澤阻，失業轉徙之民欲少復於舊，難巳！夫除其所惡，聚其所欲，塞其所害，導其所利，此固任撫綏者之責。將安其民，胡憚而久不為邪？
西北戎馬衰於簡練之不時，將臣不聞以為校也。異時邊陲失守，則勞天旨之切問，而京營將領校惰窳莫更，簡命特注，稱其任使者誰乎？法令弛而士卒玩，離次冗散之兵欲稍易於前，難巳！夫備其器械，精其技擊，謹其節制，嚴其部曲，此固任閫幕者之事。將强其兵，胡憚而久不為邪？然則舉
translation_en:
…the two capitals to oversee and govern all within the four seas. Across several thousand years, such an age has seldom been encountered. Yet when peace endures, people are prone to laxity and indolence; when ease and prosperity reach their height, the natural course of things gives greater cause for concern over excessive abundance. Thus the fiscal resources of the southeast are exhausted by limitless exactions, yet we hear of no concern from the officials responsible for finance. When people become displaced and lose their homes, the imperial treasury must be called upon to disburse relief. Now, while the agricultural colonies of the Jiang and Huai regions suffer grievously from flooding, imperial orders have repeatedly been issued: who has fulfilled the trust placed in them? The sovereign’s benevolence is obstructed, and its benefits are prevented from reaching those below. For people who have lost their livelihoods and wander from place to place, even a modest recovery of their former condition is difficult indeed! To remove what they abhor, gather what they desire, block what harms them, and open the way to what benefits them—these are surely the responsibilities of those entrusted with pacifying and reassuring the people. If they would bring the people security, what do they fear, that they have so long failed to act?
The military forces of the northwest have declined because selection and training are not conducted at the proper times, yet we hear of no effort by the commanders to examine the matter. When the frontier defenses fail, His Majesty must be troubled to issue urgent inquiries. Yet the commanders and officers [?] of the capital garrisons remain indolent and ineffectual, with no reform. His Majesty gives particular attention to their selection and appointment: who has proved worthy of the duties entrusted to him? Laws and commands are lax, and the soldiers treat them lightly. For troops who have left their posts and become idle and scattered, even a slight improvement over their former condition is difficult indeed! To provide their equipment, perfect their fighting skills, exercise care in their command and discipline, and impose strict order upon their units—these are surely the duties of those entrusted with military command and staff responsibilities. If they would strengthen their forces, what do they fear, that they have so long failed to act? Thus, to take up…

title: 嘉靖三十一年應天府鄉試錄
text:
二祖初制以作久弛之勢振中外法守以濟大
可有為之時所謂握幾御要迓
大休於無窮其道昭然有在也若夫
二京遠近堅瑕之守則今日備禦先後形要
亦居有可見者焉蓋
太祖嘗議以中都為北京矣慮土氣疎薄之弗
稱又
詔以大梁為北京矣思形勢曠遠之難用故
獨挈幽燕雄都以授封
===
神武不世出之英嗣是蓋投之以未終之業而
委之以欲究之志豈非默有所畀付者與
故永樂辛丑之詔稱創建宮室紹
皇考之先志則
二祖深思
聖子
神孫萬葉相承之基必非玆地莫可久當爾然
近嗌强胡形險既不可獨恃遠制姦宄兵
威復不可無振蓋漢立三輔强榦弱支之

punctuated: 二祖初制，以作久弛之勢，振中外法守，以濟大可有為之時，所謂握幾御要，迓大休於無窮，其道昭然有在也。若夫二京遠近堅瑕之守，則今日備禦先後形要，亦居有可見者焉。蓋太祖嘗議以中都為北京矣，慮土氣疎薄之弗稱；又詔以大梁為北京矣，思形勢曠遠之難用。故獨挈幽燕雄都，以授封神武不世出之英嗣，是蓋投之以未終之業，而委之以欲究之志，豈非默有所畀付者與？故永樂辛丑之詔稱創建宮室，紹皇考之先志，則二祖深思聖子神孫萬葉相承之基，必非玆地莫可久當爾。然近嗌强胡，形險既不可獨恃；遠制姦宄，兵威復不可無振。蓋漢立三輔，强榦弱支之
translation_en:
…the original institutions of the two founding emperors, to reinvigorate arrangements long allowed to lapse, and restore observance of the laws both at court and in the provinces, thereby making the most of an age in which great things can be accomplished: this is what is meant by grasping the critical opportunities and controlling the essentials, welcoming great blessings without end. The way to achieve this is plainly evident.

As for the defenses near and far from the two capitals, their strengths and vulnerabilities also offer indications [?] of the priorities and strategically important positions for defensive preparations today. Taizu once considered making Zhongdu the northern capital, but feared that its soil and vital influences were too poor to suit the purpose. He also decreed that Daliang should be the northern capital, but reflected that its terrain was too open and extensive to be readily used for defense. Thus he singled out the mighty metropolis of You-Yan and granted it as a fief to his outstanding heir, whose inspired martial prowess was seldom seen in any age. This was surely to entrust him with an unfinished undertaking and charge him with fulfilling an ambition not yet realized. Was this not a tacit transmission of responsibility?

Thus the decree of the xinchou year of Yongle [?] spoke of constructing palace buildings to carry forward the former intentions of his deceased imperial father. The two founding emperors therefore gave profound thought to the foundation upon which their sagely sons and divine grandsons would succeed one another for ten thousand generations; surely no place other than this could long serve that purpose. Yet, with powerful northern peoples close at the throat, the natural strength of the terrain cannot alone be relied upon; and to control malefactors at a distance, military might must also be invigorated. The Han established the Three Capital Regions, and the principle of strengthening the trunk and weakening the branches …

title: 嘉靖三十一年應天府鄉試錄
text:
道得矣今東控山海西扼紫荆皆
畿甸近壤設輔郡以列
京師之捍蔽而省上番操備之班軍則屏翰
成而邊守可强或者其一計乎唐設府兵
居重馭輕之勢全矣今內亘順天外環七
府皆
輦轂重地寓民兵以壮
國家之干城而免歲派科差之雜役則武勇
奮而畿民可寬或者其一策乎夫二事
===
先朝大臣甞惓惓列之條議今其說固猶存
也然內詆為闊論弗之行外視為難事莫
與任此深遠久長之謀所以卒抑於衆口
之紛呶矣惟今
聖天子獨化鈞陶於上賢公卿大夫左右翊贊
於下皆足以馳驅域外之議者矧二政固
在人舉而行之非難邪草茅闇陋不知所
裁幸執事教之
第二問
banxin: 順天鄉試錄 三十八

國家之干城而免歲派科差之雜役則武勇
各而畿民可寬或者其一策乎夫二事
===
祖宗朝大臣嘗惓惓列之條議今其說固猶存
也然內詆爲闊論弗之行外視爲難事莫
與任此深遠久長之謀所以卒抑於衆口
之紛呶矣惟今
聖天子獨化鈞陶於上賢公卿大夫左右翊贊
於下皆足以馳驅域外之議者矧二政固
在人舉而行之非難耶草茅闇陋不知所
裁幸執事教之
第二問
punctuated:
道得矣。今東控山海，西扼紫荆，皆畿甸近壤。設輔郡以列京師之捍蔽，而省上番操備之班軍，則屏翰成而邊守可强，或者其一計乎？唐設府兵，居重馭輕之勢全矣。今內亘順天，外環七府，皆輦轂重地。寓民兵以壮國家之干城，而免歲派科差之雜役，則武勇奮而畿民可寬，或者其一策乎？夫二事，先朝大臣甞惓惓列之條議，今其說固猶存也。然內詆為闊論，弗之行；外視為難事，莫與任。此深遠久長之謀，所以卒抑於衆口之紛呶矣。惟今聖天子獨化鈞陶於上，賢公卿大夫左右翊贊於下，皆足以馳驅域外之議者。矧二政固在人舉而行之，非難邪？草茅闇陋，不知所裁，幸執事教之。

第二問
translation_en:
…the proper way was attained. Now Shanhai is controlled to the east and Zijing guarded to the west; both lie close to the capital region. If supporting prefectures were established to form a line of defenses for the capital, and the troops serving rotating tours of training and defense were reduced, a protective bulwark would be formed and frontier defenses could be strengthened. Might this be one possible plan? The Tang established the prefectural militia system (fubing), fully realizing an arrangement in which the powerful center controlled the less powerful periphery. Now Shuntian stretches across the interior, with seven prefectures encircling it outside; all are strategically important lands surrounding the imperial capital. If militia were organized among the people to strengthen the state's defenders, and the people were exempted from the miscellaneous labor services assessed annually, martial courage would be roused and the inhabitants of the capital region relieved. Might this be one possible policy?

Ministers of earlier reigns once earnestly set out these two measures in their itemized proposals, and their arguments certainly still survive today. Yet those within the court disparage them as impractical talk and do not implement them; those outside regard them as difficult undertakings, and none will assume responsibility. This is why plans of such profound foresight and lasting benefit have ultimately been suppressed by the clamor of many voices. Now, however, the sage Son of Heaven alone directs the transforming work of government above, while worthy dukes, ministers, and grandees assist him on either side below. All are capable of putting into effect proposals reaching beyond the realm. How much more so these two policies, which depend simply upon people taking them up: surely implementing them is not difficult? An obscure and ignorant man of humble station, I do not know what judgment to make. I would be grateful for your instruction.

Second Question

title: 嘉靖三十一年應天府鄉試錄

同考試官訓導林批是策能因古今之

punctuated:
許汝驥

同考試官訓導林批：「是策能因古今之變，推出國勢人心，施於政教，皆今日之可行者。豈非適用之才乎？敬服！敬服！」

同考試官教諭鄧批：「歷代紀綱風俗之善，未有能過我國家者。然時久不能無敝，子能反覆推求其故，而有捄處之術，殆非經生之見矣。宜錄。」

考試官修撰郭批：「援古證今，非洞識化理之機者不能道。用魁本房。」

考試官右中允尹批：「能言國勢人心之出於紀綱風俗，鑿鑿皆實語。他日效用，必有所著見。錄之，不獨以文也。」

天下之勢，非政無以持之，然必先察其幾矣；天下之志，非教無以一之，然必先審其尚矣。勢之輕重，紀綱所由出焉。察其幾，使不戾於政，是故遠近得所，持而懸於上者，無偏滯不舉之患。志之媺惡，風俗所由成
translation_en:
Xu Ruji 許汝驥

Comment by Associate Examiner Lin, Assistant Instructor: “This policy essay traces changes from antiquity to the present to elucidate the configuration of power in the state and the disposition of the people's hearts, applying its conclusions to government and moral instruction. All its proposals can be implemented today. Is this not a man of practical ability? My profound admiration!”

Comment by Associate Examiner Deng, Instructor: “No previous dynasty has surpassed our own in the excellence of its governing order and popular customs. Yet, as time passes, abuses inevitably arise. You have repeatedly examined their causes and possess methods for remedying them. These are surely not merely the views of a student of the Classics. He should be selected.”

Comment by Examiner Guo, Senior Compiler: “He draws on antiquity to substantiate his account of the present. Only someone who thoroughly understands the workings of moral transformation and good government could express this. Rank him first in this examining section.”

Comment by Examiner Yin, Right Mentor: “He can explain how the configuration of power in the state and the disposition of the people's hearts arise from governing order and popular customs. Every assertion is firmly grounded in reality. When he enters service, he will certainly achieve conspicuous results. We select him for more than his writing alone.”

The configuration of power under Heaven cannot be sustained without government; yet one must first discern its incipient tendencies. The aspirations of those under Heaven cannot be unified without moral instruction; yet one must first examine what they esteem. The relative weight of power is the source from which governing order emerges. By discerning its incipient tendencies and ensuring that they do not run counter to government, both distant and nearby regions find their proper places, and the balance upheld on high suffers neither unequal weighting nor obstruction that prevents it from functioning. The goodness or badness of people's aspirations is what gives rise to popular customs…

title: 嘉靖三十一年應天府鄉試錄
text:
焉審其尚使不拂於教是故剛柔得所一
而興於下者無頹靡不振之憂二者咸順
其理矣天下庸有不大治乎夫紀綱風俗
古今論治道者所必舉以為訓要也執事
獨推本於國勢人心以明二者所從出愚
讀史觀歷代相承之變知所言有前徵矣
請據以對夫紀綱者上之所治乎下也其
名訓於詩書然非有物類之可稱者是故
欲求治天下之理必先思其故焉苟不於
===
國勢重輕之間得可制之幾以施於政則
大無所張如網之不能振其綱小無所理
如絲之不能治其紀由是懸於上者遠近
無所持而治不得其要矣風俗者下之所
化乎上也其說著於易禮然非有事形之
可指者是故欲求化天下之道必豫考其
原焉苟不於人心媺惡之中得所定之尚
以齊於教則漸靡無術其何以相動而為
風導示無方其何以相效而成俗由是興

古今論治道者所必舉以爲訓要也執事

===

大無所張如綱之不能振其綱小無所理
如絲之不能治其紀由是懸於上者遠近
無所持而治不得其要矣風俗者下之所
化乎上也其說著於易禮然非有事形之
可指者是故欲求化天下之道必豫考其
原焉苟不於人心熾惡之中得所定之尚
以齊於教則漸靡無術其何以相動而爲
風導示無方其何以相效而成俗由是興
punctuated:
焉。審其尚，使不拂於教，是故剛柔得所一，而興於下者無頹靡不振之憂。二者咸順其理矣，天下庸有不大治乎？夫紀綱風俗，古今論治道者所必舉以為訓要也。執事獨推本於國勢人心，以明二者所從出。愚讀史，觀歷代相承之變，知所言有前徵矣，請據以對。
夫紀綱者，上之所治乎下也。其名訓於《詩》《書》，然非有物類之可稱者。是故欲求治天下之理，必先思其故焉。苟不於國勢重輕之間得可制之幾，以施於政，則大無所張，如網之不能振其綱；小無所理，如絲之不能治其紀。由是懸於上者，遠近無所持，而治不得其要矣。風俗者，下之所化乎上也。其說著於《易》《禮》，然非有事形之可指者。是故欲求化天下之道，必豫考其原焉。苟不於人心媺惡之中得所定之尚，以齊於教，則漸靡無術，其何以相動而為風？導示無方，其何以相效而成俗？由是興
translation_en:
…take shape. Examine what people esteem and ensure that it does not run counter to moral instruction. Thus the firm and the yielding alike can be brought into unity, and what arises among those below will be free from the danger of decline and listlessness. When both accord with their proper principles, how could all under Heaven fail to be well governed? The ordering principles of government and the customs of the people are matters that everyone discussing the way of government, past or present, has invariably cited as essential teachings. You, sir, have particularly traced their roots to the condition of the state and the hearts of the people, thereby clarifying the sources of both. In my humble reading of history and observation of changes across successive dynasties, I have found historical precedents confirming your words. Permit me to reply on that basis.
The ordering principles of government are what those above use to govern those below. These terms are explained in the Book of Odes and the Book of Documents, yet they denote no tangible class of objects that one can name. Therefore, anyone seeking the principles for governing all under Heaven must first reflect on their underlying causes. Unless, amid the relative strength and weakness of the state, one grasps the crucial juncture at which control can be exercised and applies this understanding to government, there will be nothing to uphold the larger framework—like a net whose headrope cannot be raised—and nothing to order the smaller details—like silk threads whose strands cannot be sorted. Consequently, the authority vested above will have no means of sustaining either distant or nearby regions, and government will fail to grasp what is essential.
Customs are the ways in which those below are transformed by those above. They are discussed in the Book of Changes and the ritual classics, yet they possess no concrete form that one can point to. Therefore, anyone seeking the way to transform all under Heaven must first investigate their source. Unless, amid the goodness and badness of people's hearts, one identifies the values to be established and brings people into accord through moral instruction, there will be no method of gradually influencing them: how, then, can they influence one another to form shared ways? Without a proper means of guidance and instruction, how can they imitate one another to establish customs? Consequently, what arises…

title: 嘉靖三十一年應天府鄉試錄
text:
於下者剛柔無所一而化不從其極矣是
故古之治天下者察紀綱之能理然後其
政可舉蓋紀綱在天下猶人身之有脉也
國勢其元氣矣不察紀綱於國勢是治脉
而不先元氣也善醫者爲之乎古之化天
下者觀風俗之能同然後其教可立蓋風
俗在天下猶田疇之有稼也人心其穀種
矣不觀風俗於人心是滋稼而不亟穀種
也善耕者爲之乎昔三代治法施之政爲
===
紀綱者粲乎既無弗備至周則監二代以
成之故其政自天子至於庶人小大相承
而不亂其紀綱載之六典可考也至後世
不能舉文武之政國勢弱而莫支陵遲既
久諸侯强大天子威令下移紛然莫知所
統强力相加以至於亂也此由在上者不
察國勢重輕之幾制其政以持之故爾夫
豈先王紀綱之失哉秦代周不求其本乃
一切削其政而反之隳名城殺豪傑黜除
punctuated: 於下者，剛柔無所一，而化不從其極矣。是故古之治天下者，察紀綱之能理，然後其政可舉。蓋紀綱在天下，猶人身之有脉也；國勢，其元氣矣。不察紀綱於國勢，是治脉而不先元氣也，善醫者爲之乎？古之化天下者，觀風俗之能同，然後其教可立。蓋風俗在天下，猶田疇之有稼也；人心，其穀種矣。不觀風俗於人心，是滋稼而不亟穀種也，善耕者爲之乎？昔三代治法，施之政爲紀綱者，粲乎既無弗備。至周，則監二代以成之，故其政自天子至於庶人，小大相承而不亂，其紀綱載之六典可考也。至後世，不能舉文武之政，國勢弱而莫支。陵遲既久，諸侯强大，天子威令下移，紛然莫知所統，强力相加，以至於亂也。此由在上者不察國勢重輕之幾，制其政以持之故爾。夫豈先王紀綱之失哉？秦代周，不求其本，乃一切削其政而反之，隳名城，殺豪傑，黜除
translation_en:
…among those arising below, firmness and gentleness have no unifying standard, and moral transformation fails to attain its proper culmination. Thus those in antiquity who governed All-under-Heaven examined whether its governing framework could be put in order; only then could their administration be carried out. For the governing framework of All-under-Heaven is like the vessels of the human body, while the strength of the state is its primal vital energy. To examine the governing framework without reference to the strength of the state is to treat the vessels without first attending to the primal vital energy. Would a good physician do this? Those in antiquity who morally transformed All-under-Heaven considered whether its customs could be brought into accord; only then could their teachings be established. For customs in All-under-Heaven are like crops in the fields, while the hearts of the people are their seed grain. To consider customs without reference to the people's hearts is to nourish crops without giving priority to their seed grain. Would a good farmer do this?

Formerly, the methods of government of the Three Dynasties, as applied in administration to constitute a governing framework, were splendidly complete in every respect. When the Zhou arose, they took the two preceding dynasties as their models and brought this framework to completion. Thus, in their administration, from the Son of Heaven down to the common people, the lesser and greater ranks supported one another without disorder. Their governing framework is recorded in the Six Statutes and can be examined there. In later ages, however, rulers could no longer carry out the government of Kings Wen and Wu, and the strength of the state declined, with nothing to sustain it. After a long period of deterioration, the feudal lords became powerful, and the Son of Heaven's authority and power of command shifted downward. Amid the resulting confusion, no one knew where allegiance lay; the strong imposed their might upon others, and disorder ensued. This happened only because those above failed to discern the subtle indications of the state's relative strength and weakness and to shape their administration so as to sustain it. How could it have been a failing of the former kings' governing framework? When Qin replaced Zhou, it did not seek the root of the matter, but instead swept away Zhou's entire administration and reversed its practices, demolishing renowned fortified cities, killing outstanding men, and abolishing…

title: 嘉靖三十一年應天府鄉試錄
text:
五等滅諸侯之籍自以天下不必紀綱可
治矣然奮其詐力不再世卒仆於孤立其
視周何如也漢而後雖稍知紀綱不可廢
然變制易法大抵多懲巳敗之迹而苟且
以彌縫之國勢重輕之相懸制之不得其
幾則遠近無所持而後之不可因者猶前
也故懼孤立而封侯王則僭叛之患無與
謀抑外戚而疑功臣則閹竪之禍弗能計
其後若晉之八王唐之藩鎭宋之夷狄皆
===
懲之過而不得所矯之善國勢轉移之間
無以復制其幾欲紀綱維一代之治是元
氣未宣理期脉周一身而皆順必無幾矣
此紀綱之出於國勢不可不察者也三代

周則積數十世以興之故其敎自朝廷以
及鄕黨上下相趨以無倦其風俗詠於列

…the five ranks of nobility and erased the registers of the feudal lords, believing that All-under-Heaven could be governed without institutions and ordering principles. Yet, exerting its cunning and force, Qin ultimately fell through its isolation before two generations had passed. How did it compare with Zhou? From the Han onward, rulers gradually recognized that institutions and ordering principles could not be dispensed with. Yet in altering institutions and changing laws, they generally reacted to the traces of past failures and merely patched things up with expedients. Where the distribution of power within the state was profoundly unequal, failure to regulate it at the critical juncture left both distant and nearby regions without support. The arrangements bequeathed to successors were then no more sustainable than those that had preceded them. Thus, fearing isolation, rulers enfeoffed marquises and kings, only to find themselves with no one to consult about the resulting usurpation and rebellion. They curbed imperial relatives by marriage and distrusted meritorious ministers, yet could not foresee the calamities brought by eunuchs. Later examples—the Eight Princes of Jin, the regional military commands of Tang, and the non-Han peoples confronting Song—all arose from excessive reactions to earlier troubles that failed to achieve a sound remedy. As the balance of power shifted, rulers could no longer regain control at the critical juncture. To expect institutions and ordering principles to sustain a dynasty’s good government under these conditions was like expecting the vessels to circulate smoothly throughout the body when its vital energy had not yet been properly distributed [?]: there could be little prospect of success. This is why one must examine how institutions and ordering principles arise from the configuration of state power.
Under the Three Dynasties, transformation through the Way brought people to fulfillment, and the teachings that formed their customs were pure, with nothing that was not good. By the Zhou, efforts accumulated over several tens of generations had brought these teachings to flourishing. Thus, from the court down to local communities, those above and below followed one another tirelessly in their observance. Their customs, celebrated in the songs of the various states, can still be imagined. But later kings could no longer apply the teachings of Feng and Hao. People’s hearts became divided and could not be united. When this disintegration reached its extreme, scholars outside office freely advanced their contentious views, and the purport of the Hundred Schools…

title: 嘉靖三十一年應天府鄉試錄
text:
殊科雜然各進其說異端競起以入於邪
也此由在上者不審人心媺惡之尚齊其
教以一之故爾夫豈先王風俗之戾哉秦
併天下不揆其原乃一時欲拜黔首而愚
之阬儒生放博士燔燬諸籍屏聖人之經
自以天下盡變其風俗可久矣然擅其威
用不數十年迄危於怨集其視周何如也
漢而下雖或知風俗所當重然徇時詭習
不過少更其熟爛之軌而因循以恬安之
===
人心媺惡之相辨約之弗定其尚則剛柔
無所一而令之不可從者猶昔也故厭苛
虐而務寬厚或長讕佞之風薄阿附而崇
操節致激標榜之禍其後若晉之清談唐
之靡文宋之聲容議論皆承其偏而不得
所裁之中人心安定之後無以復易其尚
欲風俗成一代之治是穀實未種播求稼
藝百畝而皆穫必難幸矣此風俗之成於
人心不可不知者也由此觀之紀綱非能

不過少更其熟爛之軌而因循以恬安之
===
人心𢡟惡之相辨紛之弗定其尚則剛柔
無所一而今之不可從者猶昔也故厭苛
虐而務寬厚或長諂佞之風薄阿附而崇
操節致激標榜之禍其後若晉之清談唐
之靡文宋之聲容議論皆承其偏而不得
所裁之中人心安定之後無以復易其尚
欲風俗成一代之治是穀實未種播求稼
藝百畝而皆穫必難幸矣此風俗之成於
人心不可不知者也因此觀之紀綱非能
punctuated:
殊科，雜然各進其說，異端競起，以入於邪也。此由在上者不審人心媺惡之尚，齊其教以一之故爾，夫豈先王風俗之戾哉？秦併天下，不揆其原，乃一時欲拜黔首而愚之，阬儒生，放博士，燔燬諸籍，屏聖人之經，自以天下盡變其風俗，可久矣。然擅其威用，不數十年，迄危於怨集，其視周何如也？漢而下，雖或知風俗所當重，然徇時詭習，不過少更其熟爛之軌，而因循以恬安之。人心媺惡之相辨，約之弗定其尚，則剛柔無所一，而令之不可從者猶昔也。故厭苛虐而務寬厚，或長讕佞之風；薄阿附而崇操節，致激標榜之禍。其後若晉之清談，唐之靡文，宋之聲容議論，皆承其偏，而不得所裁之中。人心安定之後，無以復易其尚，欲風俗成一代之治，是穀實未種播，求稼藝百畝而皆穫，必難幸矣。此風俗之成於人心不可不知者也。
由此觀之，紀綱非能
translation_en:
…divided into different schools, each advancing its own doctrines in a confused profusion; heterodox teachings arose in competition, leading people into error. This happened because those above failed to examine the inclinations of people’s hearts toward good and evil and to bring their teachings into accord so as to unify them. How could it have been a perversion inherent in the customs of the former kings?
When Qin annexed All under Heaven, it did not consider the source of the problem. Instead, it sought at one stroke to make the common people bow down [?] and keep them ignorant. It buried Confucian scholars alive, banished Erudites, burned the various writings, and excluded the sages’ classics. It supposed that, having wholly transformed the customs of All under Heaven, it could endure for long. Yet, wielding its coercive power unchecked, within a few decades it was imperiled by accumulated resentment. How did it compare with Zhou?
From Han onward, rulers sometimes understood that customs deserved serious attention. Yet they followed the aberrant habits of their times, doing no more than slightly altering well-worn practices and complacently resting in inherited routines. In distinguishing between good and evil in people’s hearts, their attempts at restraint failed to establish settled preferences. Thus firmness and gentleness lacked a unifying standard, and commands remained as impossible to follow as before. Hence, when they rejected harsh oppression and pursued generosity and kindness, they sometimes fostered a fashion for deceit and flattery; when they disparaged servile attachment and exalted integrity, they provoked the disasters of factional acclaim. Later examples—the pure conversation of Jin, the ornate writing of Tang, and the ceremonial forms and disputations of Song—all perpetuated such one-sided tendencies without attaining the proper mean by which to regulate them. Once people’s hearts had become settled in these ways, there was no means of changing their preferences again. To expect customs then to bring about good government for an entire dynasty would be like expecting to cultivate a hundred mu and reap a harvest throughout without having sown any grain: such good fortune would surely be hard to obtain. This is what must be understood about how customs take shape in people’s hearts.
Viewed in this light, the guiding principles and disciplinary framework of government cannot…

title: 嘉靖三十一年應天府鄉試錄
text:
自理必政之作於上者有以提挈而振舉
之則國勢揚厲而不弛由是朝廷得所持
而百官承序萬民順則遠近自無敢戾法
者紀綱所以不偏滯也其輕重之持盖定
矣不然雖事事而稽之何益理亂之原邪
風俗非能自厚必教之行於下者足以化
導而移易之則人心興起而不怠由是邦
國得所效而禮教上行刑罰下清剛柔自
無弗協中者風俗所以不頹靡也其媺惡
===
之一既審矣不然雖人人而禁之何補治
忽之要邪我
國家自
二祖攘夷變夏振武修文以張無競之國勢故
紀綱虎陳譬辰象之正員樞而陰陽寒暑
經緯其運以不忒也遠近相維統體不紊
政之所持可以推萬世而無弊自古言紀
綱之善未有能過之者今
大聖踐序撫

===
忽之要邪我
國家自
二祖攘夷變夏振武修文以張無競之國勢故
紀綱虎陳譬辰象之正員樞而陰陽寒暑

政之所持可以推萬世而無弊自古言紀
綱之善未有能過之者今
大聖踐序撫
punctuated:
自理，必政之作於上者有以提挈而振舉之，則國勢揚厲而不弛。由是朝廷得所持，而百官承序，萬民順則，遠近自無敢戾法者，紀綱所以不偏滯也。其輕重之持盖定矣。不然，雖事事而稽之，何益理亂之原邪？風俗非能自厚，必教之行於下者足以化導而移易之，則人心興起而不怠。由是邦國得所效，而禮教上行，刑罰下清，剛柔自無弗協中者，風俗所以不頹靡也。其媺惡之一既審矣。不然，雖人人而禁之，何補治忽之要邪？
我國家自二祖攘夷變夏，振武修文，以張無競之國勢，故紀綱虎陳，譬辰象之正員樞，而陰陽寒暑經緯其運以不忒也。遠近相維，統體不紊，政之所持可以推萬世而無弊。自古言紀綱之善，未有能過之者。今大聖踐序，撫
translation_en:
…order themselves. Government exercised from above must take them in hand and set them firmly in motion; then the strength of the state will rise vigorously and never slacken. Thus the court gains something on which to rely, the hundred officials observe their proper order, and the myriad people follow the norms. Those near and far naturally dare not transgress the laws: this is how the governing framework avoids imbalance and stagnation. The proper balance between leniency and severity is thereby established. Otherwise, even if every affair were scrutinized, what benefit would this bring at the source of order and disorder? Customs cannot become sound of themselves. Instruction carried out among the people must suffice to transform, guide, and reform them; then people’s hearts will be stirred and will not grow indolent. Thus the realm gains a model to follow, ritual instruction prevails above, and punishments are administered justly below. Firmness and gentleness naturally accord with the mean: this is how customs avoid degeneration. The standard distinguishing their goodness and badness is thereby clearly determined. Otherwise, even if every person were subjected to prohibitions, what would this contribute to the essentials of good and negligent government?
In our dynasty, the Two Founding Ancestors drove out the barbarians and transformed the realm into a Chinese order, invigorating military power and cultivating civil accomplishments to enhance the unrivaled strength of the state. Thus the governing framework was arrayed with tiger-like majesty [?], like the celestial bodies properly aligned about the circular pivot [?], with yin and yang, cold and heat, weaving through their movements without deviation. Near and far sustain one another, and the whole remains orderly. What government upholds can be extended through ten thousand generations without ill effect. Among all the excellent governing frameworks spoken of since antiquity, none has surpassed this. Now our Great Sage has succeeded to the throne and taken charge of…

title: 嘉靖三十一年應天府鄉試錄
text:
開創之鴻圖威之所及殊方絶域惕然歸命
之恐後以此
國勢而振紀綱宜大者張而小者治內外清
和咸理彬彬無不舉之政也然
綸音屢降莫飭百司之怠理而諸章奏所陳
廢缺之當修者更僕未能究其指焉豈政
之端使然邪
列聖明倫章化崇經表訓以淑不解之人心故
風俗齊一譬嶽鎮之定方儀而南北高深
列辨其宜以不殊也故剛柔化中性情咸
則教之所被可以協四海而皆同自古言
風俗之美未有及之者今
中興建極揚
繼述之宏業德之所加羣黎百姓昭然敏化
以自新宜動乎上而感乎下吏民績理竝
敘斤斤無弗迪之教也然
訓言時敷罔觀四海之協極而諸獄訊所列
傷悖之齮化者窮年不能殫其狀焉豈教

…the grand design established at the dynasty’s founding. Wherever imperial might reaches, distant lands and remote regions submit in fearful awe, lest they be the last to acknowledge allegiance. With such strength in the state, the revitalization of its governing order should ensure that major matters are upheld and minor ones properly managed. Within and without, all should be peaceful, harmonious, and well ordered: a flourishing government in which no undertaking is neglected. Yet although imperial pronouncements repeatedly descend, they do not correct the negligence of the many offices. The neglected and deficient matters requiring repair, as set forth in the various memorials, are so numerous that even with successive attendants one could not finish examining their purport. Can some fault at the root of government have brought this about?
The successive sage emperors clarified human relationships and made moral transformation manifest, honored the classics and exalted their teachings, thereby nurturing goodness in human hearts without slackening [?]. Wherever this teaching extended, it could bring all within the four seas into concord and unity. Among all the fine customs spoken of since antiquity, none have equaled these. Now, in this restoration, the supreme standard has been established and the great enterprise of carrying forward the predecessors’ work magnified. title: 嘉靖三十一年應天府鄉試錄
text:
之□□□□天下之大政非壅而不達
也上有求治之明下無任治之良雖三王
不能以顯功今百司庶府事體紛更靡常
弊孔所漏明智弗燭利隙所開峻法莫止
當事者不敢專制攝之柄任職者不得盡
繩檢之防由是一事之施數煩
詔旨一司之掌頻費程督猶恐未得其理也欲
紀綱之振難已竊意轉動風采使國勢重
輕之幾有所制抑阻伸而幽隱達則諫諍
===
之官法紀之吏其任宜選也必得人如古
汲黯鮑宣張綱范滂者倫乎是在作之而
已矣蓋名節奮揚之際雖庸人亦可激勉
志氣隳靡之餘即豪傑有所不能振起此
自然之勢也然則國勢既賴以有制紀綱
何患不舉乎故曰先察其幾夫重輕之不
可無慎殆較然著邪兆民之衆政非尼而
不行也外有更化之名內無興化之實雖
五帝不能以施德今殊方異地氣習漸靡
punctuated:
之□□□□。天下之大政，非壅而不達也。上有求治之明，下無任治之良，雖三王不能以顯功。今百司庶府，事體紛更靡常；弊孔所漏，明智弗燭；利隙所開，峻法莫止。當事者不敢專制攝之柄，任職者不得盡繩檢之防。由是一事之施，數煩詔旨；一司之掌，頻費程督，猶恐未得其理也。欲紀綱之振，難已！竊意轉動風采，使國勢重輕之幾有所制，抑阻伸而幽隱達，則諫諍之官、法紀之吏，其任宜選也。必得人如古汲黯、鮑宣、張綱、范滂者倫乎？是在作之而已矣。蓋名節奮揚之際，雖庸人亦可激勉；志氣隳靡之餘，即豪傑有所不能振起，此自然之勢也。然則國勢既賴以有制，紀綱何患不舉乎？故曰先察其幾。夫重輕之不可無慎，殆較然著邪？
兆民之衆，政非尼而不行也。外有更化之名，內無興化之實，雖五帝不能以施德。今殊方異地，氣習漸靡
translation_en:
…[four illegible characters]. In the great affairs of governing the realm, it is not that administration is obstructed and therefore fails to reach its destination. Above there is an enlightened desire for good government; below there are no worthy men to take responsibility for governing. Even the Three Kings could not achieve manifest success under such conditions. Now, throughout the many offices and agencies, the conduct of affairs changes incessantly, without constancy. Where abuses find loopholes, even clear intelligence cannot cast light; where openings for private gain appear, even stringent laws cannot stop them. Those in charge dare not exercise sole authority over control and supervision; those holding office cannot fully enforce the safeguards of rules and restraints. Thus, implementing a single matter repeatedly troubles the throne for decrees, and the responsibilities of a single office repeatedly require regulation and supervision; yet there is still fear that affairs have not been properly ordered. How difficult it is to restore governing discipline!
I humbly think that, to inspire a vigorous bearing and bring under control the critical factors that strengthen or weaken the state—so that the suppressed may find expression and what is hidden may become known—the officials charged with remonstrance and those responsible for law and discipline should be carefully selected for their posts. Must we obtain men of the company of the ancients Ji An, Bao Xuan, Zhang Gang, and Fan Pang [?]? It depends simply on rousing them. For when reputation and integrity are vigorously upheld, even ordinary men can be inspired to exert themselves; once resolve and spirit have fallen into decay, even outstanding men may be unable to rouse themselves. This is the natural tendency of things. If the strength of the state is thereby brought under control, why worry that governing discipline will not be restored? Hence the saying: first examine the critical factors. Is it not quite apparent that the strengthening and weakening of the state must be treated with care?
Among the multitude of the common people, it is not that administration is impeded and therefore fails to operate. Outwardly there is the name of reforming moral influence; inwardly there is no substance to making that influence flourish. Even the Five Emperors could not extend their virtue under such conditions. Now, in far-flung regions and different localities, dispositions and customs are gradually declining…

title: 嘉靖三十一年應天府鄉試錄
text:
相循仁讓之風比閭弗興貪殘之化草縫
首競長民者踐身教之方當塗者乏人倫
之表由是進取得規攘袂爭赴筐篋可溢
褫冠弗顧猶恐未饜其志也欲風俗之善
難已竊意建樹儀則使人心嫐惡之趨有
所定頑鈍易而集詬恥則禮教之臣師帥
之職其授宜擇也欲得人如古石建疏廣
文翁黃霸者比乎亦在重之而已矣蓋徃
弊柘襲之久雖曠日改之而不足上志推
===
隆之専則一二人倡之而有餘此亦必然
之効也然則人心旣因以有變風俗何憂
不厚乎故曰先審其尚夫嫐惡之不可無
重蓋昭然明邪雖然二者其道相成其效
未始不相應也蓋國勢人心因於上下而
不違故紀綱風俗成於政教而不戾其本
要必有在爾昔董仲舒言於漢以師異道
人異論則上亡以持一統法制數變下不
知所守此言不齊教以一人心則紀綱不
punctuated:
相循，仁讓之風比閭弗興，貪殘之化草縫首競。長民者踐身教之方，當塗者乏人倫之表。由是進取得規，攘袂爭赴，筐篋可溢，褫冠弗顧，猶恐未饜其志也。欲風俗之善，難已！竊意建樹儀則，使人心嫐惡之趨有所定，頑鈍易而集詬恥，則禮教之臣、師帥之職，其授宜擇也。欲得人如古石建、疏廣、文翁、黃霸者比乎？亦在重之而已矣。蓋徃弊柘襲之久，雖曠日改之而不足；上志推隆之専，則一二人倡之而有餘，此亦必然之効也。然則人心旣因以有變，風俗何憂不厚乎？故曰先審其尚。夫嫐惡之不可無重，蓋昭然明邪！
雖然，二者其道相成，其效未始不相應也。蓋國勢人心因於上下而不違，故紀綱風俗成於政教而不戾，其本要必有在爾。昔董仲舒言於漢，以師異道人異論，則上亡以持一統，法制數變，下不知所守。此言不齊教以一人心，則紀綱不
translation_en:
…follow one another in this. A spirit of benevolence and deference fails to arise among the neighborhoods, while the influence of greed and cruelty prompts a scramble to take the lead among the common people [?]. Those who govern the people practice instruction by personal example [?], yet those in power lack the exemplary conduct required by human relationships. Consequently, people make advancement and gain their rule [?], rolling up their sleeves and competing to rush ahead. They fill their baskets and chests to overflowing, heedless of losing their official caps, and still fear that their ambitions remain unsatisfied. How difficult it is to make customs good!
I venture to think that standards of conduct should be established, so that people’s preferences and aversions [?] have a settled direction and the stubborn and dull may change and acquire a sense of shame [?]. Accordingly, appointments as ministers responsible for ritual instruction and as teachers and leaders should be made selectively. Do we wish to obtain men comparable to Shi Jian, Shu Guang, Wen Weng, and Huang Ba of antiquity? This too depends simply on according such offices due importance. When inherited abuses have long been perpetuated [?], even prolonged efforts at reform prove insufficient. But when the ruler’s resolve is devoted to honoring and promoting these standards, one or two men taking the lead will more than suffice. This, too, is an inevitable result. Once people’s hearts have thereby changed, why worry that customs will fail to become sound? Hence I say: first examine what is esteemed. Surely it is plainly evident that preferences and aversions [?] must be treated as matters of consequence!
Nevertheless, these two approaches complement each other, and their effects invariably correspond. The strength of the state and the hearts of the people depend upon those above and below acting without discord; thus institutional order and social customs are formed through government and instruction without conflict. Their essential foundation must lie somewhere. Formerly, Dong Zhongshu told the Han court that, when teachers followed different ways and people espoused different opinions, those above had no means of maintaining unity; laws and institutions changed repeatedly, and those below did not know what to observe. This means that, unless instruction is unified so as to unite the hearts of the people, institutional order cannot…

title: 嘉靖三十一年應天府鄉試錄
text:
可振矣朱熹言於宋謂賢否上下必辨功
罪刑賞必明萬事之統無所缺則天下之
人矜奮勸勉各自去惡而從善此言不修
政以張國勢則風俗不可善矣是故宮府
之政整攝於上國勢得所持而紀綱可振
風俗之所以善也庠序之教畫一於下人
心得所定而風俗可成紀綱之所以明也
詩所謂勉勉我王紀綱四方記所謂一道
德以同俗紀綱既正天下大定者皆合二
===
物而究言之者也術之可舉化之可更其
事武不出是雖然此皆
今日達而有位者之任衡蘿賤士又何敢與
說焉
第三問
同考試官教諭譚　批　顧名世
宜此策推考詳覈辨析著明且能敷說我
國家制治重守令之意子非達政體者乎高薦何疑
封建郡縣古今
punctuated:
可振矣。朱熹言於宋，謂賢否上下必辨，功罪刑賞必明，萬事之統無所缺，則天下之人矜奮勸勉，各自去惡而從善。此言不修政以張國勢，則風俗不可善矣。是故宮府之政整攝於上，國勢得所持而紀綱可振，風俗之所以善也；庠序之教畫一於下，人心得所定而風俗可成，紀綱之所以明也。《詩》所謂「勉勉我王，紀綱四方」，《記》所謂「一道德以同俗」，「紀綱既正，天下大定」者，皆合二物而究言之者也。術之可舉，化之可更，其事武不出是。雖然，此皆今日達而有位者之任，衡蘿賤士又何敢與說焉？

第三問

同考試官教諭譚，批。顧名世。

宜此策推考詳覈，辨析著明，且能敷說我國家制治重守令之意。子非達政體者乎？高薦何疑？

封建郡縣古今
translation_en:
…be revitalized. Zhu Xi, addressing the Song court, said that the worthy and unworthy must be distinguished in assigning higher and lower positions, and that merit and guilt, punishments and rewards, must be clearly determined. If nothing is lacking in the overall ordering of affairs, the people throughout the realm will rouse themselves and encourage one another, each abandoning evil and following goodness. This means that unless government is improved so as to strengthen the state, customs cannot be made good. Thus, when the administration of the palace and government offices is properly ordered and regulated above, the strength of the state is sustained and its governing framework can be revitalized: this is how customs are made good. When instruction in the schools is unified below, people’s hearts are steadied and good customs can be established: this is how the governing framework is made clear. The Book of Odes says, “Diligent is our king, ordering the four quarters”; the Book of Rites says, “Unify moral principles to make customs alike,” and “Once the governing framework is rectified, all under Heaven is firmly settled.” All these statements consider the two together and explain them fully. The methods that may be put into effect and the transformations that may be brought about do not, in practice [?], extend beyond this. Nevertheless, these are all responsibilities of those who have attained office today. How could a lowly scholar such as myself [?] dare take part in discussing them?

Third Question

Comment by Associate Examiner Tan, Instructor. Candidate: Gu Mingshi.

Fitting indeed [?]: this policy essay investigates thoroughly and precisely, and its distinctions and analyses are clear. Moreover, it expounds our dynasty’s intention in governing the realm by placing great weight on prefects and county magistrates. Are you not someone who understands the principles of government? Why hesitate to recommend you highly?

Enfeoffment and the commandery-and-county system, in antiquity and today…

title: 嘉靖三十一年應天府鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教諭林　批
國家分治守令是專然能不負其任者亦難得是子反覆推說詳
我
同考試官學正陳　批
歷古今其志可概見矣取冠本房允宜
能變通古制推美
考試官修撰郭　批
今法詞意眞切若慨然不忘時瘼者必有志之士也
守令近民在政最切是子
考試官右中允尹　批
發明賞用非區區章句之學者錄之
守令一問人人能答之據
實可行無如此作
===
法不必古制之求也在能安其民政不必
徃法之議也在能任其官是故民苟安其
法矣雖變古不足以爲戾官苟任其賢矣
雖更法不足以爲撓夫封建者先王公天
下之制也然以施今時必不能興治欲求
安民古可專尚乎師其意不泥其迹今未
嘗不古之從耳郡縣者後世順天下之法
也然以稽徃代亦無不宜於政不知任官
法可徒議乎擇其賢使稱其職政未嘗不
punctuated:
同考試官教諭林批：國家分治，守令是專，然能不負其任者亦難得。是子反覆推說詳我。
同考試官學正陳批：歷古今，其志可概見矣。取冠本房，允宜。能變通古制，推美。
考試官修撰郭批：今法，詞意眞切，若慨然不忘時瘼者，必有志之士也。守令近民，在政最切。是子。
考試官右中允尹批：發明賞用，非區區章句之學者，錄之。守令一問，人人能答之，據實可行，無如此作。
法不必古制之求也，在能安其民；政不必徃法之議也，在能任其官。是故民苟安其法矣，雖變古不足以爲戾；官苟任其賢矣，雖更法不足以爲撓。夫封建者，先王公天下之制也，然以施今時，必不能興治。欲求安民，古可專尚乎？師其意，不泥其迹，今未嘗不古之從耳。郡縣者，後世順天下之法也，然以稽徃代，亦無不宜於政。不知任官，法可徒議乎？擇其賢，使稱其職，政未嘗不
translation_en:
Comment by Associate Examiner Lin, Instructor: The state divides the work of government, entrusting it specifically to prefects and magistrates; yet those capable of fulfilling their responsibilities are hard to find. This candidate develops his argument repeatedly and in detail [?].
Comment by Associate Examiner Chen, School Director: Surveying antiquity and the present, one can broadly discern his aspirations. It is entirely fitting to rank him first in this examination section. He can adapt ancient institutions and extol [?].
Comment by Examiner Guo, Senior Compiler: Present institutions [?]. His language and meaning are sincere and apt. He seems deeply moved, never forgetting the afflictions of the age; he must be a man of resolve. Prefects and magistrates are close to the people and are of the most immediate importance in government. This candidate [?].
Comment by Examiner Yin, Right Companion to the Heir Apparent: He elucidates rewards and appointments [?]; his learning is not confined to petty explication of textual phrases. Accept him. Everyone can answer a question about prefects and magistrates, but for grounding its proposals in reality and making them practicable, no essay equals this one.
In establishing laws, one need not seek ancient institutions; what matters is being able to bring peace to the people. In governing, one need not debate former laws; what matters is being able to appoint the proper officials. Thus, if the people live peacefully under the laws, even departing from antiquity need not constitute a violation; if worthy men are appointed to office, even changing the laws need not constitute a disruption. Now, enfeoffment was the institution through which the former kings shared the realm with others. Yet if applied today, it would certainly fail to produce good government. If one seeks to bring peace to the people, can antiquity alone be esteemed? Follow its intent without clinging to its outward forms: present practice has never ceased to follow antiquity in this sense. The system of commanderies and counties was a method by which later ages accommodated the circumstances of the realm. Yet, examining past dynasties, it was also invariably suitable for government. If one does not understand how to appoint officials, can merely debating laws suffice? Choose worthy men and ensure that they are equal to their posts: government has never failed to…

title: 嘉靖三十一年應天府鄉試錄
text:
人之因耳執事感封建郡邑之變慨然思
今守令欲得其人以成天下之理化可謂
識制治之先要矣顧非承學所究知者然
言及之不敢以默焉夫封建肇自古始黄
帝以來厥迹稍列於傳記唐虞三代之制
則詩書班班可考已晝野而列其疆域分
土而胙之封爵上秉侯度以承天子使一
人之職貢無所闕下執藩屏以匡諸夏使
四方之變亂有所制在易水比於地先王
===
以建萬國親諸侯蓋王者比民猶地之比
水夫比水不以衆川則羣流之奔赴無所
入比民不以諸侯則萬姓之歸趨無所附
矣故曰聖人公天下之制也夫三代相傳
至周之始興也諸侯碁列中外猶千八百
國焉其後王綱中弛伯强力政列國自相
殘滅於是離十二以併於七封建之初制
蕩亡矣然則黜除五等放絕先王之制豈
獨秦人之始事邪裂諸侯之地而郡縣之
punctuated: 人之因耳。執事感封建郡邑之變，慨然思今守令，欲得其人以成天下之理化，可謂識制治之先要矣。顧非承學所究知者，然言及之，不敢以默焉。夫封建肇自古始，黄帝以來，厥迹稍列於傳記；唐虞三代之制，則詩書班班可考已。晝野而列其疆域，分土而胙之封爵，上秉侯度以承天子，使一人之職貢無所闕；下執藩屏以匡諸夏，使四方之變亂有所制。在易，水比於地，先王以建萬國，親諸侯。蓋王者比民，猶地之比水。夫比水不以衆川，則羣流之奔赴無所入；比民不以諸侯，則萬姓之歸趨無所附矣。故曰聖人公天下之制也。夫三代相傳，至周之始興也，諸侯碁列中外，猶千八百國焉。其後王綱中弛，伯强力政，列國自相殘滅，於是離十二以併於七，封建之初制蕩亡矣。然則黜除五等，放絕先王之制，豈獨秦人之始事邪？裂諸侯之地而郡縣之，
translation_en:
…depend on men. You, honored sir, reflecting on the change from enfeoffment to commanderies and counties, earnestly consider the prefects and county magistrates of today and wish to obtain suitable men to accomplish orderly government and moral transformation throughout the realm. You may indeed be said to understand the foremost requirements of establishing good government. This is, however, beyond what I, a humble student, have thoroughly understood; yet, since the matter has been raised, I dare not remain silent.

Enfeoffment originated in antiquity. From the time of Huangdi onward, traces of it appear here and there in transmitted accounts. The institutions of Tang, Yu, and the Three Dynasties can be clearly examined in the Book of Odes and the Book of Documents. They marked out the countryside [?] and delineated territorial boundaries, divided the land, and bestowed it along with noble ranks. In serving above, the lords upheld the rules governing their station and attended upon the Son of Heaven, ensuring that none of the duties and tribute owed to the sovereign went unfulfilled. In acting below, they served as protective barriers to sustain the Chinese states, ensuring that disturbances in every quarter could be checked. In the Book of Changes, water cleaves to the earth; the former kings accordingly established the myriad states and drew the feudal lords close to them. The king’s drawing the people close is like the earth’s drawing water close. If water were not brought together through the many rivers, the rushing streams would have nowhere to enter; if the people were not brought together through the feudal lords, the myriad families would have nowhere to attach themselves as they sought allegiance. Hence it is called the sages’ institution for sharing the realm with all.

This system was transmitted through the Three Dynasties. When the Zhou first arose, the feudal lords were arrayed like pieces on a game board throughout the inner and outer territories, and there were still eighteen hundred states. Subsequently, royal authority slackened, and powerful hegemons governed by force. The states ravaged and extinguished one another, becoming divided into twelve and then consolidated into seven; the original institutions of enfeoffment were utterly swept away. Thus, was abolishing the five ranks of nobility and casting aside the institutions of the former kings something first undertaken by Qin alone? To divide up the lands of the feudal lords and turn them into commanderies and counties…

title: 嘉靖三十一年應天府鄉試錄
text:
蓋亦勢之不得不然者也昔曹冏言於魏
曰三代之君與天下共民故天下同其憂
秦王獨制其民故傾危莫之救後儒因謂
封建可支變故此亦未明於往勢之說矣
夫秦罷侯置守縣統以令其法雖不若先
王之公然上下相維亦自可制變遏亂茍
其後能持以善政卽何至傾危不可救也
哉是故漢繼承之設刺史守相二千石萬
户長吏郡縣之制後世遂相循莫改易焉
===
柳宗元曰封建非聖人意也勢也郡縣公
也公自秦人始其言旣偏失難據信至列
利害得失之效以爲周自東遷不振大抵
皆末大不掉之患秦有叛人無叛吏漢有
叛國無叛郡唐有叛將無叛州皆郡縣之
計得也夫自上古積數十聖人制爲公天
下之法傳之幾千百年無變豈反不若秦
人茍且旦夕之爲者邪蓋古者制民之產
井田非封建不久立國之疆封建非井田
punctuated:
蓋亦勢之不得不然者也。昔曹冏言於魏曰：「三代之君與天下共民，故天下同其憂；秦王獨制其民，故傾危莫之救。」後儒因謂封建可支變故，此亦未明於往勢之說矣。夫秦罷侯置守，縣統以令，其法雖不若先王之公，然上下相維，亦自可制變遏亂。茍其後能持以善政，卽何至傾危不可救也哉？是故漢繼承之，設刺史、守相、二千石、萬户長吏，郡縣之制，後世遂相循莫改易焉。
柳宗元曰：「封建非聖人意也，勢也。郡縣，公也，公自秦人始。」其言旣偏失，難據信。至列利害得失之效，以爲周自東遷不振，大抵皆末大不掉之患；秦有叛人，無叛吏；漢有叛國，無叛郡；唐有叛將，無叛州，皆郡縣之計得也。夫自上古積數十聖人，制爲公天下之法，傳之幾千百年無變，豈反不若秦人茍且旦夕之爲者邪？蓋古者制民之產，井田非封建不久；立國之疆，封建非井田
translation_en:
…was probably also something that circumstances made unavoidable. Cao Jiong once said to the ruler of Wei: “The rulers of the Three Dynasties shared governance of the people with all under Heaven, so all under Heaven shared their concerns. The king of Qin alone controlled his people, so when his rule tottered, no one came to its rescue.” Later scholars consequently argued that enfeoffment could withstand upheavals. This, too, is an argument that fails to understand the circumstances of the past. Qin abolished the feudal lords and appointed governors, placing counties under magistrates. Although this system was less public-spirited than that of the former kings, its higher and lower levels sustained one another, and it could in itself contain upheavals and check disorder. Had its successors maintained it through good government, how could it have reached a state of peril beyond rescue? Thus Han inherited it, establishing regional inspectors, governors and chancellors, officials ranked at two thousand bushels, and senior officials over ten thousand households [?]. Later ages continued to follow the commandery-and-county system without changing it.
Liu Zongyuan said: “Enfeoffment arose not from the sages’ intention, but from circumstances. Commanderies and counties serve the public good; this public-mindedness began with the men of Qin.” These statements are already biased and mistaken, and can hardly be accepted as trustworthy. When he enumerates the results—the advantages and disadvantages, successes and failures—he argues that Zhou failed to recover after its eastward migration largely because its extremities had become too large to control; that Qin had rebellious people but no rebellious officials; Han had rebellious kingdoms but no rebellious commanderies; and Tang had rebellious generals but no rebellious prefectures. He regards all these as successes of the commandery-and-county system. Yet from high antiquity onward, several dozen sages successively fashioned a system for holding all under Heaven in common, transmitting it unchanged for thousands of years. Could it actually have been inferior to the makeshift expedients of the men of Qin? In antiquity, when regulating the people’s livelihoods, the well-field system could not endure without enfeoffment; when establishing the territorial bounds of states, enfeoffment without the well-field system…

title: 嘉靖三十一年應天府鄉試錄
text:
不固彼不原聖人政法相維之深意以爲
封建皆屈於勢之弗能去而非其意之所
欲從則可爲妄億度爲說者矣夫聖人因
時立政如使後秦漢有作則何必獨封建
而後治哉故爲曹冏柳宗元之論者皆非
明於理亂之故而通於古今之勢者矣我
國家自
祖宗創制備善全美斟酌三代監裁百王事可
變易以宜民雖唐虞有所不襲也矧封建
===
更久遠弗復者乎然盤石之宗百世相維
意未始不相通矣法可因承以制世雖秦
漢有所不廢也矧郡縣更久遠弗易者乎
然方嶽之司諸省肝轄法未嘗不獨詳矣
是故藩國享有爵土不得預政事之權親
而貴之愛而富之則敦睦之道得豈若魏
制之而傷恩晉縱之而長亂者比邪郡縣
明其職守不得肆貪殘之虐量材官之因
能任之則選授之典公豈若秦峻其法而
punctuated:
不固。彼不原聖人政法相維之深意，以爲封建皆屈於勢之弗能去，而非其意之所欲從，則可爲妄億度爲說者矣。夫聖人因時立政，如使後秦漢有作，則何必獨封建而後治哉？故爲曹冏、柳宗元之論者，皆非明於理亂之故而通於古今之勢者矣。
我國家自祖宗創制，備善全美，斟酌三代，監裁百王。事可變易以宜民，雖唐虞有所不襲也，矧封建更久遠弗復者乎？然盤石之宗，百世相維，意未始不相通矣。法可因承以制世，雖秦漢有所不廢也，矧郡縣更久遠弗易者乎？然方嶽之司，諸省肝轄，法未嘗不獨詳矣。是故藩國享有爵土，不得預政事之權；親而貴之，愛而富之，則敦睦之道得，豈若魏制之而傷恩、晉縱之而長亂者比邪？郡縣明其職守，不得肆貪殘之虐；量材官之，因能任之，則選授之典公，豈若秦峻其法而
translation_en:
…cannot be secure. Those who fail to trace the sages’ profound intention in making governmental institutions and laws mutually sustaining, and suppose that enfeoffment was entirely a concession to circumstances that made it impossible to abolish, rather than something the sages themselves wished to pursue, may be called people who construct arguments from reckless conjecture. The sages established government according to the times. Had a sage arisen after the Qin and Han, why would order have required enfeoffment alone? Thus those who advance arguments like those of Cao Jiong and Liu Zongyuan neither understand the causes of order and disorder nor comprehend the circumstances of past and present.
In our dynasty, the founding ancestors established institutions complete in goodness and perfection, weighing the practices of the Three Dynasties and drawing critically upon the example of the hundred kings. Where practices could be changed to benefit the people, some were not adopted even from the ages of Tang Yao and Yu Shun. How much more so with enfeoffment, which has gone still longer without restoration? Yet the imperial kinsmen, firm as bedrock, sustain one another through a hundred generations: the underlying intention has never ceased to accord with that of enfeoffment. Where laws could be inherited to govern the world, some were retained even from the Qin and Han. How much more so with the commandery and county system, which has endured still longer without alteration? Yet for the offices governing the regions and the jurisdictions of the various provinces [?], the regulations have always been particularly detailed.
Thus the princely domains enjoy titles and lands but may not participate in the exercise of governmental authority. By treating the princes as kin and honoring them, loving them and enriching them, the proper way of fostering family concord is attained. How could this be compared with Wei, which restrained its princes and thereby injured familial affection, or Jin, which indulged them and thereby fostered disorder? In the commanderies and counties, officials’ duties are clearly defined, and they may not give free rein to rapacity and cruelty. By appointing them to office according to their talents and entrusting them with responsibilities according to their abilities, the rules of selection and appointment are made impartial. How could this be compared with Qin, which made its laws severe and …

title: 嘉靖三十一年應天府鄉試錄
text:
興二漢重其職而殃民者比邪蓋天下治
統於一政法伸縮在
朝廷非下之所敢擅也事舉其大生民利害
在郡縣非上之所悉知也是故樹長吏於
郡縣則政法可下達而不窒矣寄吾民於
守令則利害可上聞而不壅矣漢儒董仲
舒之言曰守令民之師帥所使承流宣化
者也師帥不賢則主德不宣恩澤不流是
安得不重其官邪考之在昔漢當文景之
===
盛君以恭儉成業而紀無可載之事臣以
質直效職而傳無可書之功其時郡守有
吳公者治行為天下第一史猶竟失其名
他若孟舒魏尚田叔之輩皆斤斤信實治
郡之聲聞天下然記錄之文不一論著其
行能則上下之相勉於實何如也是以郡
國幾致刑措民終壽考嬉游若小兒狀乃
後武帝以多慾耗天下臣下化之貪殘之
風競熾直指刺察之使交道不足易其所
punctuated: 興，二漢重其職而殃民者比邪？蓋天下治統於一，政法伸縮在朝廷，非下之所敢擅也；事舉其大，生民利害在郡縣，非上之所悉知也。是故樹長吏於郡縣，則政法可下達而不窒矣；寄吾民於守令，則利害可上聞而不壅矣。漢儒董仲舒之言曰：「守令，民之師帥，所使承流宣化者也。師帥不賢，則主德不宣，恩澤不流。」是安得不重其官邪？考之在昔，漢當文景之盛，君以恭儉成業，而紀無可載之事；臣以質直效職，而傳無可書之功。其時郡守有吳公者，治行為天下第一，史猶竟失其名。他若孟舒、魏尚、田叔之輩，皆斤斤信實，治郡之聲聞天下，然記錄之文不一論著其行能，則上下之相勉於實何如也？是以郡國幾致刑措，民終壽考，嬉游若小兒狀。乃後武帝以多慾耗天下，臣下化之，貪殘之風競熾，直指刺察之使交道，不足易其所
translation_en:
…provoked unrest [?], or with the two Han dynasties, which invested these offices with great authority yet brought calamity upon the people? For the governance of All-under-Heaven is unified under a single authority. The tightening or relaxation of policies and laws rests with the court; those below dare not decide such matters on their own. Yet, to speak of the essentials, the benefits and harms affecting the people's livelihood lie with the commanderies and counties, and those above cannot know them all. Thus, by establishing senior officials in the commanderies and counties, policies and laws can reach those below without obstruction; by entrusting our people to prefects and magistrates, their benefits and hardships can be reported upward without impediment. The Han scholar Dong Zhongshu said: “Prefects and magistrates are the people's teachers and leaders, charged with receiving the influence of the ruler and spreading his transforming instruction. If these teachers and leaders are unworthy, the ruler's virtue is not made manifest, and his beneficence does not flow forth.” How, then, could these offices fail to be treated as important?

Looking back to the flourishing Han reigns of Emperors Wen and Jing, the rulers accomplished their work through reverence and frugality, yet the annals had no notable events to record; their ministers fulfilled their duties with integrity and straightforwardness, yet their biographies had no notable achievements to recount. Among the commandery governors of that time was one Master Wu, whose administrative performance ranked first in the empire, yet the historical record ultimately failed even to preserve his personal name. Others, such as Meng Shu, Wei Shang, and Tian Shu, were all scrupulous, trustworthy, and sincere, and their reputations for governing commanderies were known throughout the empire. Yet the written records did not set out their conduct and abilities individually. How devoted, then, were those above and below to encouraging one another in substantive achievement! Thus the commanderies and kingdoms nearly reached the point at which punishments could be laid aside, and the people lived out their full span of years, roaming at leisure like little children. Later, however, Emperor Wu exhausted the empire through his many desires. His ministers followed his example, and greed and cruelty spread ever more fiercely. Investigating emissaries charged with direct scrutiny crowded the roads, but they were insufficient to change what …

title: 嘉靖三十一年應天府鄉試錄
text:
漸靡也宣帝起於民間知守令近民於治
最要重故慨然思良二千石欲與之共治
天下時推擇其賢者引對殿陛問民疾苦
而其召賜黃金擢拜大司農之殊典亦前
此所未有也是以一時守令莫不爭先奮
效而循良吏著稱於史彬彬焉今觀班史
所列西漢之吏六人則黃霸朱邑王成龔
遂文翁召信臣是已而其時若汲黯董仲
舒蕭望之輩則固未嘗一著其賢焉范史
所述東漢之吏十二人則衛颯任延王景
之秦彭王渙許荊孟嘗劉寵第五倫童恢
劉矩仇覽是已而其時若劉昆魯恭卓茂
輩則固未嘗一載其能焉至若唐之吏傳
不錄狄仁傑宋璟韓愈諸人宋之吏傳不
錄包拯歐陽脩蘇軾諸人蓋要其大節不
卓卓於一事推其全能不沾沾於一郡作
史者義例固各有當也而豈一循吏之述
足概其平生哉我
punctuated: 漸靡也。宣帝起於民間，知守令近民，於治最要重，故慨然思良二千石，欲與之共治天下。時推擇其賢者，引對殿陛，問民疾苦，而其召賜黃金、擢拜大司農之殊典，亦前此所未有也。是以一時守令莫不爭先奮效，而循良吏著稱於史，彬彬焉。今觀班史所列西漢之吏六人，則黃霸、朱邑、王成、龔遂、文翁、召信臣是已。而其時若汲黯、董仲舒、蕭望之輩，則固未嘗一著其賢焉。范史所述東漢之吏十二人，則衛颯、任延、王景之、秦彭、王渙、許荊、孟嘗、劉寵、第五倫、童恢、劉矩、仇覽是已。而其時若劉昆、魯恭、卓茂輩，則固未嘗一載其能焉。至若唐之吏傳，不錄狄仁傑、宋璟、韓愈諸人；宋之吏傳，不錄包拯、歐陽脩、蘇軾諸人。蓋要其大節，不卓卓於一事；推其全能，不沾沾於一郡。作史者義例固各有當也，而豈一循吏之述足概其平生哉？我
translation_en:
…the corrupting influence that had gradually taken hold. Emperor Xuan rose from among the common people and knew that commandery governors and county magistrates, being close to the people, were of the utmost importance to government. He therefore earnestly sought worthy officials of the two-thousand-bushel rank, wishing to govern the empire together with them. From time to time he selected the worthy among them, summoned them to audience at the palace, and asked about the people's hardships. The exceptional honors he bestowed—summoning an official and granting him gold, or promoting him to Minister of Revenue—were likewise unprecedented. Thus the governors and magistrates of the time all strove to take the lead in devoted service, and a splendid array of conscientious and benevolent officials won renown in the histories.

Now, the six Western Han officials listed in Ban Gu's history are Huang Ba, Zhu Yi, Wang Cheng, Gong Sui, Wen Weng, and Shao Xinchen. Yet the worthiness of such contemporaries as Ji An, Dong Zhongshu, and Xiao Wangzhi was never recorded there. The twelve Eastern Han officials described in Fan Ye's history are Wei Sa, Ren Yan, Wang Jingzhi [?], Qin Peng, Wang Huan, Xu Jing, Meng Chang, Liu Chong, Diwu Lun, Tong Hui, Liu Ju, and Qiu Lan. Yet the abilities of such contemporaries as Liu Kun, Lu Gong, and Zhuo Mao were never recorded there. Similarly, the biographies of exemplary officials in the Tang histories do not include Di Renjie, Song Jing, Han Yu, and others; those in the Song histories do not include Bao Zheng, Ouyang Xiu, Su Shi, and others. For, considering their integrity in its essential aspects, their distinction was not confined to a single deed; assessing the full range of their abilities, they were not content with achievements in a single commandery. Historians' principles of classification each have their own justification. How could a single account of an exemplary official suffice to encompass such a man's entire life? Our…

title: 嘉靖三十一年應天府鄉試錄
text:
聖祖高皇帝勤恤民隱深思時艱作
大誥以訓天下若陳希文之執法不阿王復
春之陳諫不避何敏中李善之歷陳弊政
陸鑑之禁劾旗軍皆顯書其行能以示勸
臣民當時士大夫之仕有職守者感激
聖明之知被則爲之必致其力矜勉
訓言之昭獎則居之必竭其能此數人不必
著列古循吏之林而一代誦其治行所得
已過漢吴公遠矣今我
===
聖天子敷求迪哲之良愼簡親民之吏屢
詔所司申重其選凡布列天下當守令長治
之任者科目士十居八九焉夫俊傑之彥
撫時以奮功名豈弟之良得位以施仁澤
天下元元之蒙被康休者固不少矣乃或
特士間出於儔倫中人易參於俗化志行
貪殘上阻
朝廷之德厚才性闇劣下爲閭閻之害患敢
謂今之郡縣無若人矣哉蓋嘗聞之元儒
punctuated:
聖祖高皇帝勤恤民隱，深思時艱，作《大誥》以訓天下。若陳希文之執法不阿、王復春之陳諫不避、何敏中李善之歷陳弊政、陸鑑之禁劾旗軍，皆顯書其行能，以示勸臣民。當時士大夫之仕有職守者，感激聖明之知被，則爲之必致其力；矜勉訓言之昭獎，則居之必竭其能。此數人不必著列古循吏之林，而一代誦其治行，所得已過漢吴公遠矣。
今我聖天子敷求迪哲之良，愼簡親民之吏，屢詔所司申重其選。凡布列天下當守令長治之任者，科目士十居八九焉。夫俊傑之彥，撫時以奮功名；豈弟之良，得位以施仁澤，天下元元之蒙被康休者固不少矣。乃或特士間出於儔倫，中人易參於俗化，志行貪殘，上阻朝廷之德厚；才性闇劣，下爲閭閻之害患。敢謂今之郡縣無若人矣哉？蓋嘗聞之元儒
translation_en:
… the sagely progenitor, Emperor Gao, diligently attended to the people's hidden sufferings and pondered deeply the difficulties of the age. He composed the Grand Pronouncements (Da Gao) to instruct the realm. Such deeds as Chen Xiwen's impartial enforcement of the law, Wang Fuchun's fearless remonstrance, He Minzhong's and Li Shan's detailed exposition of abuses in government, and Lu Jian's restraint and impeachment of banner troops were all prominently recorded as examples of conduct and ability, to encourage officials and subjects. The scholar-officials then holding offices with defined responsibilities, moved by the enlightened sovereign's recognition and favor, devoted their full strength to their duties. Encouraged to earnest effort by the conspicuous praise in his instructions, they exhausted their abilities in office. These men need not have been ranked among the exemplary officials of antiquity: an entire age celebrated their administrative conduct, and the recognition they gained already far surpassed that of Lord Wu of the Han.
Now our sage Son of Heaven searches widely for worthy men of wisdom and carefully selects officials who deal directly with the people, repeatedly commanding the responsible authorities to give renewed weight to their selection. Of those appointed throughout the realm to serve as prefects and county magistrates, eight or nine in ten are men recruited through the examinations. Outstanding men seize the opportunities of their times to achieve distinction; kindly and gracious men obtain office and extend benevolent care. Surely no small number of the common people throughout the realm have thus enjoyed peace and well-being. Yet exceptional men emerge only occasionally from among their peers, while ordinary men readily drift with prevailing customs. Those whose purposes and conduct are greedy and cruel obstruct the court's generous beneficence above; those whose abilities and dispositions are benighted and inferior bring harm and distress upon the common people below. Dare we claim that today's prefectures and counties contain no such men? I have heard from a Yuan-dynasty Confucian scholar …

title: 嘉靖三十一年應天府鄉試錄
text:
吳臨川所述有五善三欺之說是雖治民
嘗言然能以五善勉己則無不可行之政
三欺馭衆則無不可燭之情推之四方無
弗宜矣況一郡縣乎又嘗聞之宋儒呂東
萊所持有三事一忍之戒是雖當官通律
然能以三事愼修則守定而事可周一忍
中制則德弘而謀有濟措之百司無弗通
矣況一守令乎漢章帝之詔有曰俗吏矯
飾外貌以許爲察以刻爲明以輕爲德以
重爲威四者行則下有怨心爲之愈勤亂
===
之愈長嗚呼有味哉其言之也夫四者非
古今政人所當通戒者邪是故士誠以澤
民利物爲心則一夫不獲危於疾痛之迫
身而況吾所分理之民邪學誠以行道濟
時爲志則一事失理切於患害之加己而
況吾所當治之政邪雖然古語有之清法
之國人畏法而不畏吏亂法之國人畏吏
而不畏法夫法者聖人所以磨厲天下之
punctuated: 吳臨川所述，有五善三欺之說。是雖治民嘗言，然能以五善勉己，則無不可行之政；三欺馭衆，則無不可燭之情。推之四方，無弗宜矣，況一郡縣乎？又嘗聞之宋儒呂東萊所持，有三事一忍之戒。是雖當官通律，然能以三事愼修，則守定而事可周；一忍中制，則德弘而謀有濟。措之百司，無弗通矣，況一守令乎？漢章帝之詔有曰：「俗吏矯飾外貌，以許爲察，以刻爲明，以輕爲德，以重爲威。四者行，則下有怨心；爲之愈勤，亂之愈長。」嗚呼！有味哉，其言之也！夫四者，非古今政人所當通戒者邪？是故士誠以澤民利物爲心，則一夫不獲，危於疾痛之迫身，而況吾所分理之民邪？學誠以行道濟時爲志，則一事失理，切於患害之加己，而況吾所當治之政邪？雖然，古語有之：「清法之國，人畏法而不畏吏；亂法之國，人畏吏而不畏法。」夫法者，聖人所以磨厲天下之
translation_en:
…in the writings of Wu of Linchuan, there is a discussion of the five good practices and the three deceptions. Although these are commonplace teachings on governing the people, if one uses the five good practices to spur oneself onward, no measure of government will be impossible to carry out; if one governs the multitude with an understanding of the three deceptions, no circumstance will be beyond illumination. Applied throughout the realm, they are everywhere appropriate—how much more so in a single prefecture or county! I have also heard that the Song Confucian Lü of Donglai upheld the admonition concerning three matters and one act of forbearance. Although these are general rules for holding office, if one diligently cultivates oneself through the three matters, one’s principles will remain firm and affairs can be handled comprehensively; if one exercises forbearance with proper restraint, one’s virtue will broaden and one’s plans will succeed. Applied throughout the many offices, they are everywhere effective—how much more so for a single prefect or magistrate!

An edict of Emperor Zhang of the Han says: “Commonplace officials put on a false outward appearance, taking assent for discernment [?], harshness for perspicacity, leniency for virtue, and severity for authority. When these four practices prevail, those below harbor resentment; the more diligently officials pursue them, the more disorder grows.” Ah, how meaningful these words are! Are these four practices not things against which those who govern, past and present alike, should guard? Thus, if a scholar truly sets his heart on benefiting the people and all things, the failure of even one man to find his proper place will alarm him more than illness and pain afflicting his own body. How much more must this be so for the people entrusted to his administration! If, in learning, he truly aims to put the Way into practice and meet the needs of his age, a single matter handled contrary to principle will concern him more keenly than harm befalling himself. How much more must this be so for the affairs he is charged with governing!

Nevertheless, an old saying has it: “In a state where the laws are clear, people fear the laws but do not fear officials; in a state where the laws are disordered, people fear officials but do not fear the laws.” Now, the laws are that by which the sages hone and temper all under Heaven…

title: 嘉靖三十一年應天府鄉試錄
text:
具也法不清則才且賢者不得所奮興而
頑鄙不肖之人迄莫知顧而畏也夫我
國家之制郡縣守令之分治其境也有藩伯
以統之則政出於一不得徇一吏之從違
有監司以臨之則吏齊乎法不得恣一夫
之好惡而內臺撫按之臣取諸衆論以列
賢不肖之薦劾大宰專攝其衡柄御史大
夫總飭其綱維凡所薦劾近則取決於議
覆遠則需定於覲察所爲法旣備且詳矣
乃今守令有淑慝未盡旌別善惡未盡章
癉者則亦法未有以淸之之過耳夫頑鄙
不肖者之莫知顧畏由贓吏之禁罰未嚴
而才賢者之不得所奮興則良吏之未有
以振其激勸之具耳蓋
===
祖宗治贓吏之法甚重今洪武永樂初法縱未
能皆舉行獨未可嚴治其一二以爲天下
之極懲乎乃若激勸之具則今天下縣令
而賢也旣得入補臺省銓司之任然獨止
punctuated: 具也。法不清，則才且賢者不得所奮興，而頑鄙不肖之人迄莫知顧而畏也。夫我國家之制，郡縣守令之分治其境也，有藩伯以統之，則政出於一，不得徇一吏之從違；有監司以臨之，則吏齊乎法，不得恣一夫之好惡。而內臺撫按之臣，取諸衆論，以列賢不肖之薦劾；大宰專攝其衡柄，御史大夫總飭其綱維。凡所薦劾，近則取決於議覆，遠則需定於覲察。所爲法旣備且詳矣，乃今守令有淑慝未盡旌別、善惡未盡章癉者，則亦法未有以淸之之過耳。夫頑鄙不肖者之莫知顧畏，由贓吏之禁罰未嚴；而才賢者之不得所奮興，則良吏之未有以振其激勸之具耳。蓋祖宗治贓吏之法甚重，今洪武永樂初法縱未能皆舉行，獨未可嚴治其一二，以爲天下之極懲乎？乃若激勸之具，則今天下縣令而賢也，旣得入補臺省銓司之任，然獨止
translation_en: …the instrument for doing so. If the laws are not clear, capable and worthy men have no opportunity to exert themselves and rise, while obstinate, base, and unworthy men never learn caution or fear. Under our dynasty’s institutions, prefects and magistrates administer their respective jurisdictions under Provincial Administration Commissioners. Government thus proceeds from a single authority and cannot accommodate an individual official’s compliance or resistance. Surveillance officials oversee them, bringing officials into conformity with the law and preventing any one man from indulging his personal likes and dislikes. The officials of the central Censorate, together with Grand Coordinators and Regional Inspectors, draw upon public opinion to submit recommendations of the worthy and impeachments of the unworthy. The Minister of Personnel has sole charge of weighing their merits, while the Censor-in-chief exercises overall supervision of discipline. Recommendations and impeachments are decided in the nearer term through deliberation and review, or await settlement at the court-audience evaluations. The laws established for these purposes are already comprehensive and detailed. Yet among today’s prefects and magistrates, the upright and the corrupt are not all distinctly recognized, nor are the good and the wicked all duly commended and punished. This is simply the fault of failing to make the laws clear. That obstinate, base, and unworthy men know neither caution nor fear results from insufficiently strict prohibitions and penalties against corrupt officials. That capable and worthy men lack opportunities to exert themselves and rise results from the failure to invigorate the means of encouraging good officials. The ancestral emperors’ laws for punishing corrupt officials were exceedingly severe. Even if the early laws of the Hongwu and Yongle reigns cannot now all be put into effect, could we not deal severely with one or two such officials as an emphatic warning to all under Heaven? As for the means of encouragement, worthy county magistrates throughout the realm can now be brought into central service to fill posts in the Censorate, the ministries, and the personnel selection offices. Yet this is restricted solely to…

title: 嘉靖三十一年應天府鄉試錄
text:
於進士之塗耳若夫爲郡守者卽有古潁
川渤海之政上所以優擢之者亦不過藩
臬一佐僚止耳夫漢制部刺史高第卽得
遷爲郡守郡守高第卽得入爲九卿
國初在外郡守之良亦往往召入爲部侍郎
夫是以人自勉於力善高行殊能之士不
能不拔出於群衆人之表也我
皇上踐阼初年亦每於大覲時銓司特推郡守
之賢者
===
命錫宴部堂以寵之今茲典不可一二間行
以爲激勸之微權乎其若縣令之補內職
要在人稱其才不當問所出之塗官因其
人不宜計所循之資則凡擢臺省銓司之
官又何必拘拘進士之流而不及他塗之
選抑奇傑跅弛之氣使不得一伸吐於繩
尺操制之外邪壅愚之見抒陳槩略不識
執事以爲何如
第四問
punctuated:
於進士之塗耳。若夫爲郡守者，卽有古潁川、渤海之政，上所以優擢之者，亦不過藩臬一佐僚止耳。夫漢制，部刺史高第，卽得遷爲郡守；郡守高第，卽得入爲九卿。國初，在外郡守之良，亦往往召入爲部侍郎。夫是以人自勉於力善，高行殊能之士，不能不拔出於群衆人之表也。我皇上踐阼初年，亦每於大覲時，銓司特推郡守之賢者，命錫宴部堂以寵之。今茲典不可一二間行，以爲激勸之微權乎？其若縣令之補內職，要在人稱其才，不當問所出之塗；官因其人，不宜計所循之資。則凡擢臺省銓司之官，又何必拘拘進士之流，而不及他塗之選，抑奇傑跅弛之氣，使不得一伸吐於繩尺操制之外邪？壅愚之見，抒陳槩略，不識執事以爲何如？

第四問
translation_en:
…to those who entered through the metropolitan graduate (jinshi) route alone.
