As for prefects, even if their administration matches that of the ancient exemplars of Yingchuan and Bohai, the preferential promotion granted them by the throne amounts to no more than an assistant post in a Provincial Administration Commission or Provincial Surveillance Commission. Under the Han system, a Regional Inspector with a superior performance rating could be promoted to commandery governor, and a commandery governor with a superior rating could enter the central government as one of the Nine Chamberlains. At the beginning of our dynasty, good prefects serving outside the capital were also frequently summoned to become Vice Ministers. Thus men spurred themselves to strive for good government, and those of lofty conduct and exceptional ability could not fail to distinguish themselves from the multitude.

In the early years after our Emperor ascended the throne, whenever the grand audience was held, the personnel authorities would specially recommend worthy prefects, and he would order banquets bestowed upon them in the ministry hall as a mark of favor. Could this practice not now be observed once or twice from time to time, as a modest means of encouragement? As for appointing district magistrates to posts in the central government, the essential thing is that the appointee's abilities suit the position; one should not inquire by what route he entered service. Offices should be assigned according to the person, without calculating the seniority he has accumulated. Thus, when promoting men to posts in the Censorate, the central ministries, and the personnel administration, why must selection be rigidly confined to metropolitan graduates, excluding candidates from other routes? Why suppress the spirit of extraordinary, unrestrained men, preventing it from finding even a single outlet beyond the constraints of prescribed rules? I have set forth the broad outline of my benighted views [?]; I do not know what you, sir, think of them.

Fourth Question

title: 嘉靖三十一年應天府鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教諭周　批〔考古而不蔓論今〕
〔而不迂謂子為俊傑士非邪〕
考試官修撰郭　批〔我〕
皇上修舉農鹽大政誠恤民濟邊之要務也子能詳悉言之可謂留
心于經世矣故錄
考試官右中允尹　批〔農鹽二政我〕
皇上特設憲臣經理蓋欲復
祖宗之舊法也是答能達其意且考據明悉有變通之術可謂難矣
厚民有道抑末以強本民可厚矣利國有
道捐近以計遠國無弗利矣本者何民所
恃以為生者是已不知所強則末能害之
欲以厚民猶反樹而求茂也遠者何國所
資以為久者是已不知所計則近能阻之
欲以利國猶却步而索前也夫三代而上
言厚民之本務莫重乎農三代而下言利
國之遠計莫大乎鹽古今論政所必首及
之者矣
punctuated:
同考試官教諭周批〔考古而不蔓，論今而不迂，謂子為俊傑士，非邪？〕

考試官修撰郭批〔我〕皇上修舉農鹽大政，誠恤民濟邊之要務也。子能詳悉言之，可謂留心于經世矣，故錄。

考試官右中允尹批〔農鹽二政，我〕皇上特設憲臣經理，蓋欲復祖宗之舊法也。是答能達其意，且考據明悉，有變通之術，可謂難矣。

厚民有道，抑末以強本，民可厚矣；利國有道，捐近以計遠，國無弗利矣。本者何？民所恃以為生者是已。不知所強，則末能害之，欲以厚民，猶反樹而求茂也。遠者何？國所資以為久者是已。不知所計，則近能阻之，欲以利國，猶却步而索前也。夫三代而上，言厚民之本務，莫重乎農；三代而下，言利國之遠計，莫大乎鹽。古今論政所必首及之者矣。
translation_en:
Comment by Associate Examiner Zhou, Instructor: “You examine antiquity without rambling and discuss the present without impracticality. Is it not right to call you a man of outstanding ability?”

Comment by Examiner Guo, Senior Compiler: “Our Emperor’s restoration and implementation of the great policies concerning agriculture and salt are indeed essential undertakings for caring for the people and provisioning the frontiers. You can discuss them thoroughly and in detail, showing that you have applied your mind to statecraft. Hence this answer is selected.”

Comment by Examiner Yin, Right Mentor: “For the two policies concerning agriculture and salt, our Emperor has specially appointed censorial officials to oversee their administration, intending thereby to restore the established regulations of his imperial ancestors. This answer grasps that intention; moreover, its examination of the evidence is clear and thorough, and it offers methods of adapting to circumstances. Such an achievement is indeed rare.”

There is a way to enrich the people: restrain the secondary occupations to strengthen the root, and the people can prosper. There is a way to benefit the state: relinquish immediate gains to plan for the long term, and the state cannot fail to benefit. What is the root? It is that upon which the people depend for their livelihood. If one does not know what to strengthen, the secondary occupations can harm it. Seeking thereby to enrich the people is like planting a tree upside down and expecting it to flourish. What is the long term? It is that upon which the state depends for its endurance. If one does not know what to plan for, immediate concerns can obstruct it. Seeking thereby to benefit the state is like stepping backward while trying to advance. From the Three Dynasties back into antiquity, among the fundamental undertakings for enriching the people, none was more important than agriculture. From the Three Dynasties onward, among long-term plans for benefiting the state, none was greater than salt. These are matters that discussions of government, ancient and modern alike, must address first.

title: 嘉靖三十一年應天府鄉試錄
text:
天子采酌羣言修明二政其安內攘外之盛
業乎愚生窮居草澤私懷當世之隱慮敢
不因明問述所知以對夫農政先王嘗備
之官矣遂師遂人遂大夫興田職務治其稼事
稼器稼法以辨耕耨種類之施蓋無不效
其勤也然是時井田之法爲民制之非專
歛其賦以充上者自秦用商鞅之謀開阡
陌重賦稅決裂疆畮則三代計民授田之
業壞由是經界失正勞民勸相之政無所
===
復行民始恣末淫而蹈奇袤其極也秦人
令民之術弃莫之或舉矣此抑末强本之
道欲厚民者不可無重也鹽法先王嘗治
之吏矣鹽人掌鹽政令共其苦鹽形鹽散
鹽以周祭祀賔客之用蓋無不致其察也
然是時山澤之利與民公之非私擢其利
以佐國者自齊用管仲之計伐菹薪煑海
水苛筭鍾釜則三代通無濟有之利塞由
是采用有禁因天制地之道無所從施民
punctuated:
天子采酌羣言，修明二政，其安內攘外之盛業乎！愚生窮居草澤，私懷當世之隱慮，敢不因明問，述所知以對？

夫農政，先王嘗備之官矣。遂師、遂人、遂大夫，興田職，務治其稼事、稼器、稼法，以辨耕耨種類之施，蓋無不效其勤也。然是時井田之法，爲民制之，非專歛其賦以充上者。自秦用商鞅之謀，開阡陌，重賦稅，決裂疆畮，則三代計民授田之業壞。由是經界失正，勞民勸相之政無所復行，民始恣末淫而蹈奇袤。其極也，秦人令民之術，弃莫之或舉矣。此抑末强本之道，欲厚民者不可無重也。

鹽法，先王嘗治之吏矣。鹽人掌鹽政令，共其苦鹽、形鹽、散鹽，以周祭祀賔客之用，蓋無不致其察也。然是時山澤之利，與民公之，非私擢其利以佐國者。自齊用管仲之計，伐菹薪，煑海水，苛筭鍾釜，則三代通無濟有之利塞。由是采用有禁，因天制地之道無所從施，民
translation_en:
The Son of Heaven gathers and weighs the many opinions, putting these two branches of administration into good order: is this not a magnificent undertaking to secure the realm internally and repel threats from without? A humble student living in obscurity among the common people, I privately harbor deep concerns about our times. How could I fail to respond to your discerning question by setting forth what I know?

As for agricultural administration, the former kings once provided a full complement of officials for it. The assistants, directors, and grand masters of the outlying districts promoted agricultural duties, attending diligently to farming operations, implements, and methods, and distinguishing the appropriate practices for plowing, weeding, and the various kinds of crops. None failed to exert himself. Yet in those days the well-field system was established for the people; it did not serve solely to collect their taxes to fill the coffers of their rulers. When Qin adopted Shang Yang’s proposal, opened up the field boundaries, increased taxation, and broke apart the boundaries of the fields, the Three Dynasties’ undertaking of allocating land according to the population was destroyed. Thereafter, field boundaries lost their proper order, and policies for encouraging the people and assisting their labors could no longer be practiced. The people began to indulge excessively in secondary occupations and pursue strange excesses [?]. In the end, Qin’s methods of directing the people were abandoned, with no one restoring them [?]. This principle of restraining secondary occupations and strengthening agriculture, the fundamental occupation, must be given due weight by anyone seeking to enrich the people.

As for the salt system, the former kings once appointed officials to administer it. The salt officials managed its regulations and supplied bitter salt, crystalline salt, and loose salt to meet the needs of sacrifices and the reception of guests. None failed to exercise careful oversight. Yet in those days the benefits of mountains and marshes were shared with the people; their profits were not appropriated exclusively to support the state. When Qi adopted Guan Zhong’s plan, cutting marsh vegetation for fuel, boiling seawater, and exacting harsh levies measured in zhong and fu, the benefits enjoyed under the Three Dynasties through circulating supplies between those who lacked them and those who possessed them were obstructed [?]. Thereafter, restrictions were imposed on gathering and using these resources, leaving no scope to apply the principle of following Heaven’s conditions and making orderly use of the earth. The people…

title: 嘉靖三十一年應天府鄉試錄
text:
者施巧法以罔貸利其弊也齊人權用之
資兼無所取效矣此損近計遠之策欲利
國者不可無究也且夫取應期會不顧萬
民之本業者必無救於內散之憂校利尋
尺不思百年之遠圖者必無制於外削之
患此少知治體者所不事而豈厚民利國
之經要乎惟我
聖祖當創造天下之始戎馬之事方驅騖而首
命帥臣興近地之農政是故流移得所招
集四方之歸從如市也其時萬民末技無
===
所用何假政令抑之乎本業既强則安內
之績所由成其效固著明矣暨平定方內
之後邊陲之備正講求而遂按往法定諸
司之鹽課是故漕輓類於關中衆商之邁
赴若流水也其時九府羨利無所私何計
纖微征之乎邊儲益盛則攘外之威所由
振其績可指見矣夫時殊政易三代聖王
之施於民者既非後世所能用則足國强
punctuated: 者施巧法以罔貸利，其弊也，齊人權用之資兼無所取效矣。此損近計遠之策，欲利國者不可無究也。且夫取應期會，不顧萬民之本業者，必無救於內散之憂；校利尋尺，不思百年之遠圖者，必無制於外削之患。此少知治體者所不事，而豈厚民利國之經要乎？惟我聖祖當創造天下之始，戎馬之事方驅騖，而首命帥臣興近地之農政。是故流移得所招集，四方之歸從如市也。其時萬民末技無所用，何假政令抑之乎？本業既强，則安內之績所由成，其效固著明矣。暨平定方內之後，邊陲之備正講求，而遂按往法定諸司之鹽課。是故漕輓類於關中，衆商之邁赴若流水也。其時九府羨利無所私，何計纖微征之乎？邊儲益盛，則攘外之威所由振，其績可指見矣。夫時殊政易，三代聖王之施於民者，既非後世所能用，則足國强
translation_en:
…those who employ ingenious devices to ensnare people through lending for profit [?]. Such are its abuses that even the resources available to the people of Qi for expedient use can no longer produce results [?]. This is a policy of sacrificing immediate gains to plan for the distant future; anyone wishing to benefit the state must examine it thoroughly. Moreover, those who exact revenues to meet deadlines without regard for the fundamental livelihood of the people will certainly have no remedy for the danger of internal disintegration. Those who calculate gains by the fathom and the foot, without considering plans for a hundred years ahead, will certainly have no means of checking the danger of encroachment from abroad. Even those with some slight understanding of the principles of government would not engage in such practices. How could these be the essential means of enriching the people and benefiting the state?
When our sagely founding ancestor first established his rule over the realm, military campaigns were still being vigorously pursued, yet he first ordered his commanders to promote agricultural administration in nearby areas. Thus displaced people were gathered and settled, and those coming from all quarters to submit to him thronged like a marketplace. At that time, the people's subsidiary occupations had no scope for employment; what need was there to suppress them by government orders? Once the fundamental occupation of agriculture was strengthened, the achievement of internal peace followed. Its effects were indeed manifest.
After the realm had been pacified, preparations for the frontiers were being carefully considered, and he accordingly followed earlier precedents to establish salt revenues for the various offices. Thus grain transport by water and land resembled that of Guanzhong, and merchants flocked there like flowing water. At that time, the surplus profits of the nine treasury offices were not appropriated for private gain; what need was there to calculate and exact the smallest sums? As frontier reserves grew more abundant, the power to repel external threats was thereby enhanced. The achievements can plainly be seen.
Now, times differ and policies change. Since what the sage kings of the Three Dynasties implemented for the people could no longer be applied by later generations, then, as for enriching the state and strengthening…

title: 嘉靖三十一年應天府鄉試錄
text:
本管商二子之告其君者抑豈
今日可得而盡棄之哉蓋款之誅秦也以三
晉磽陿有耕之民無其地關中饒廣有耕
之地無其民故誘三晉之人利其力俾復
三世無知兵事視所能任不限晦數之多
寡由是他國之民耕於內秦地之民戰於
外饟餽相資功首相扞秦之富强無敵於
天下蓋有以致之是雖首壞井田均民之
公然所以治其國中不可謂無術豈若後
===
世縱民於末淫莫知所省憂者邪管仲之
相齊也以海王之國正其鹽筴則倍利必
歸於上渠展之鹽致其本事則饋食必重
於列國故用人數而明以重相推之術習
農功而設近海聚庸之禁塞人之利鹽其
所由出之塗使見予之形不見其所奪之
理故言利出一孔者國無敵出二孔者兵
不詘九合諸侯一匡天下齊之霸威取定
於一國蓋有所成之是雖首失山澤弛利
punctuated: 本，管商二子之告其君者，抑豈今日可得而盡棄之哉？蓋款之誅秦也，以三晉磽陿，有耕之民，無其地；關中饒廣，有耕之地，無其民。故誘三晉之人，利其力，俾復三世，無知兵事，視所能任，不限晦數之多寡。由是他國之民耕於內，秦地之民戰於外，饟餽相資，功首相扞。秦之富强，無敵於天下，蓋有以致之。是雖首壞井田均民之公，然所以治其國中，不可謂無術。豈若後世縱民於末淫，莫知所省憂者邪？管仲之相齊也，以海王之國，正其鹽筴，則倍利必歸於上；渠展之鹽，致其本事，則饋食必重於列國。故用人數而明以重相推之術，習農功而設近海聚庸之禁，塞人之利鹽其所由出之塗，使見予之形，不見其所奪之理。故言利出一孔者，國無敵；出二孔者，兵不詘。九合諸侯，一匡天下，齊之霸威取定於一國，蓋有所成之。是雖首失山澤弛利
translation_en:
…the foundations: could the counsel that Guan Zhong and Shang Yang gave their rulers possibly be discarded altogether today? When Shang Yang governed Qin [?], he considered that the lands of the Three Jin were barren and cramped: they had people to cultivate the soil but lacked land. Guanzhong was fertile and extensive: it had land to cultivate but lacked people. He therefore attracted people from the Three Jin to make use of their labor, granting them exemption from service for three generations and freeing them from military affairs. The land assigned matched what they could manage, without restriction on the number of mu [?]. Thus people from other states cultivated within Qin, while Qin’s own people fought abroad. Provisions supplied mutual support, and military achievements and defense sustained one another [?]. There were thus means by which Qin attained wealth and strength unmatched anywhere under Heaven. Although this first destroyed the equity of the well-field system, which treated the people equally, its methods of governing the state cannot be said to have lacked ingenuity. How could it be compared with later ages, when people were allowed to indulge excessively in secondary occupations, with no one knowing to reflect upon or be concerned about this?

When Guan Zhong served as chief minister of Qi, he regulated the salt monopoly of a state whose maritime resources enabled it to attain supremacy, ensuring that the multiplied profits accrued to the ruler. By attending to the basic work of producing the salt of Quzhan [?], he ensured that supplies of provisions carried particular weight among the states. Thus he used population figures to elucidate a method of calculating through relative prices [?], promoted familiarity with agricultural work, and established prohibitions on gathering hired labor near the sea [?]. He blocked the channels through which people profited from salt, making them see the appearance of his giving without seeing how he took from them. Hence the saying: ‘When profit issues through one opening, the state has no rival; when it issues through two openings, its armies are not subdued.’ He assembled the regional lords nine times and brought order to all under Heaven. Qi’s might as hegemon was secured through measures within a single state: there were means by which this was accomplished. Although this was the first departure from allowing free access to the benefits of mountains and marshes…

title: 嘉靖三十一年應天府鄉試錄
text:
之仁然所以推於天下不可謂無道豈若
後世括利爲私奉不知所節恤者邪蓋秦之
首開田賦以擅利者後世師其智終莫之
能改矣惟漢文景以恭儉承業數下重農
之詔故海內庶富幾致刑措後乃耗於武
帝之征伐然末年輪臺輿悔遂封丞相爲
富民侯言方今之務在力農得趙過爲搜
粟都尉教代田耦耜之法始行太常三輔
既得菁畮多收之效終推居延邊郡益獲
===
省牛省力之便至孝昭時流民稍還田野
多蓄積之利其事可想矣今過法列於班
史推其意以施行之非長民者所有事乎
頃者言官興議
皇上銳然采用山東淮南之間特設都御史充
營田招撫之使蓋百數十年始一見者也
顧事理叢蹟羣臣所議之條雖若詳至乃
猶有首利未興舉者則亦當事之臣所宜
及時先計之也夫今寇臣經理之地沃野
punctuated:
之仁，然所以推於天下，不可謂無道，豈若後世括利爲私奉，不知所節恤者邪？蓋秦之首開田賦以擅利者，後世師其智，終莫之能改矣。惟漢文景以恭儉承業，數下重農之詔，故海內庶富，幾致刑措。後乃耗於武帝之征伐，然末年輪臺輿悔，遂封丞相爲富民侯，言方今之務在力農。得趙過爲搜粟都尉，教代田耦耜之法，始行太常、三輔，既得菁畮多收之效，終推居延邊郡，益獲省牛省力之便。至孝昭時，流民稍還，田野多蓄積之利，其事可想矣。今過法列於班史，推其意以施行之，非長民者所有事乎？
頃者言官興議，皇上銳然采用，山東、淮南之間，特設都御史充營田招撫之使，蓋百數十年始一見者也。顧事理叢蹟，羣臣所議之條雖若詳至，乃猶有首利未興舉者，則亦當事之臣所宜及時先計之也。夫今寇臣經理之地，沃野
translation_en:
…benevolence. Yet the means by which he extended his influence throughout the realm cannot be said to have lacked the Way. How could he be compared to those of later ages who scraped together profits for their private enjoyment, knowing neither restraint nor concern for the people? Qin first instituted the land tax to monopolize its revenues; later ages took its cleverness as their model, and ultimately none could change it. Only Emperors Wen and Jing of Han carried on their inherited enterprise with reverence and frugality, repeatedly issuing edicts that gave priority to agriculture. Thus the realm became populous and prosperous, and punishments nearly fell into disuse. Later, Emperor Wu’s campaigns exhausted these resources. In his final years, however, he expressed remorse over Luntai [?], and thereupon enfeoffed his Counsellor-in-Chief as Marquis for Enriching the People, declaring that the pressing task of the time was to devote effort to agriculture. He obtained Zhao Guo’s services as Commandant for Grain Collection. Zhao taught the methods of alternating fields and paired plowing, first introducing them on lands administered by the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and in the Three Metropolitan Districts. Having secured increased harvests from the cultivated fields [?], he eventually extended the methods to Juyan and the frontier commanderies, gaining the further advantages of saving oxen and labor. By Emperor Xiaozhao’s time, displaced people gradually returned, and the countryside enjoyed substantial gains in accumulated stores. We can readily imagine the circumstances. Zhao Guo’s methods are now recorded in Ban Gu’s History of the Han. Is it not the responsibility of those who govern the people to extend their underlying principles and put them into practice?
Recently, the remonstrance officials raised this proposal, and His Majesty resolutely adopted it. A Censor-in-Chief was specially appointed to serve as commissioner for establishing agricultural settlements and for recruiting and pacifying settlers in the region of Shandong and Huainan. This was an undertaking seen for the first time in well over a hundred years. Yet the affairs involved are intricate [?]. Although the provisions discussed by the assembled officials appear detailed and comprehensive, there are still primary benefits [?] that have not been developed. These, too, are matters that the officials responsible ought to plan for in advance and in good time. Now, the territory being managed by Minister Kou [?] comprises fertile plains…

title: 嘉靖三十一年應天府鄉試錄
text:
千餘里皆古諸侯所用致富强者若魏晉正
始中鄧艾嘗即其地導淮潁之水穿渠數
百里溉田之利晉世受之故我
聖祖因立都水營田司首諭兵亂隄防頹圮民
廢耕耘專令督興水利使蓄洩得宜而旱
潦有備然則營田之務水利莫先焉而䟽
議乃弗之及何也夫平原廣隰不藉溝洫
之利則旱無所瀦潦無所洩或極於延望潦無
所洩溢流將蕩於無際民之始阽流亡既
由之矣可不思善其終哉今宜以農官掌
===
水利之政課其殿最使會要有所稽成考
其勤𢡟使力作有所董正而憲臣謹察田
功必以水利為先要歲月廵歷視其地爲
之指使賞罰信明因其人爲之勸懲由是
毆撫復之民俾之樂集南畝而末游之業
禁不以妨耕稼則農政庶有興乎故曰抑
末以强本民可厚矣非此其先要邪齊重
禁鹽利以修富者後世承其術既莫之能
punctuated:
千餘里，皆古諸侯所用致富强者。若魏晉正始中，鄧艾嘗即其地導淮潁之水，穿渠數百里，溉田之利，晉世受之。故我聖祖因立都水營田司，首諭兵亂隄防頹圮、民廢耕耘，專令督興水利，使蓄洩得宜，而旱潦有備。然則營田之務，水利莫先焉，而䟽議乃弗之及，何也？夫平原廣隰，不藉溝洫之利，則旱無所瀦，潦無所洩；或極於延望，潦無所洩，溢流將蕩於無際。民之始阽流亡，既由之矣，可不思善其終哉？今宜以農官掌水利之政，課其殿最，使會要有所稽成；考其勤𢡟，使力作有所董正。而憲臣謹察田功，必以水利為先要，歲月廵歷，視其地爲之指使；賞罰信明，因其人爲之勸懲。由是毆撫復之民，俾之樂集南畝，而末游之業禁，不以妨耕稼，則農政庶有興乎！故曰：「抑末以强本，民可厚矣。」非此其先要邪？
齊重禁鹽利以修富者，後世承其術，既莫之能
translation_en:
…over a thousand li, all land by which the ancient feudal lords attained wealth and strength. During the Zhengshi era of Wei–Jin [?], for example, Deng Ai diverted the waters of the Huai and Ying rivers there and dug canals extending several hundred li; the Jin dynasty enjoyed the resulting benefits of irrigation. Thus our Sagely Founder established the Directorate of Waterways and Agricultural Colonies. His initial instructions stated that warfare had left the dikes in ruins and the people had abandoned cultivation. He specifically ordered the supervision and development of waterworks, so that water would be stored and released appropriately and preparations made against drought and flooding. In managing agricultural colonies, then, nothing takes precedence over water control. Why do the memorials discussing the matter fail to address it? On broad plains and extensive lowlands, without the benefits of irrigation and drainage channels, there is no stored water for drought and no outlet for floodwater. Sometimes, as far as the eye can see [?], floodwater has no outlet, and the overflow sweeps boundlessly across the land. This was already what first drove the people to the brink of displacement. Can we fail to consider how to bring their plight to a satisfactory conclusion? Agricultural officials should now be entrusted with water administration and graded on their performance, so that their achievements can be verified in administrative summaries [?]. Their diligence should be examined [?], so that agricultural labor receives supervision and direction. Censorial officials should carefully inspect agricultural work, invariably making water control their foremost concern. They should conduct regular inspection tours, issuing instructions suited to the terrain, and administer rewards and punishments reliably and clearly, encouraging or disciplining people according to their conduct. In this way, the people who have been pacified and restored to their homes can be directed to gather gladly in the southern fields. If subsidiary and itinerant occupations are prohibited from interfering with cultivation, agricultural administration may indeed flourish! Thus it is said: “Restrain subsidiary pursuits to strengthen the fundamental occupation, and the people can attain prosperity.” Is this not the foremost requirement?
Qi enriched itself by imposing strict controls on the profits from salt. Later ages inherited its methods, and none could …

title: 嘉靖三十一年應天府鄉試錄
text:
廢矣惟漢昭宣以賢良建說閒止榷煑之
令故利澤流下庶民休息後復罷於元帝
之初元狄踰年鹽官仍設則禁令迄與古
今相終始歷代減弛無幾煑鬻復興至唐
乃以劉晏爲鹽鐵使上鹽法輕重之議其
始鹽入歲才四十萬緡末乃至六百萬緡
幾當天下賦稅之半暨大曆末公私充羡
軍國資運濟之需其利蓋盛布矣今晏事
詳於本傳要其術而酌參之非司鹺者所
===
當心乎頃者計臣列疏
皇上慨然興行兩淮二浙之閒特設都御史任
整理鹽法之計蓋百數十年不幾遺者也
然初法久失計臣所陳之具多按舊故其
猶備失未修舉者則亦司鹺之臣所當通
變而議之也夫今憲臣所整理之方鹽利
數十倍天下古邊郡所全資其飛輓者昔
宋雍熙中令商輸芻粟於塞特優其直倍
給以江淮之鹽支兵之計宋迄賴之故我
punctuated:
廢矣。惟漢昭宣以賢良建說，閒止榷煑之令，故利澤流下，庶民休息。後復罷於元帝之初元，狄踰年鹽官仍設，則禁令迄與古今相終始。歷代減弛無幾，煑鬻復興。至唐，乃以劉晏爲鹽鐵使，上鹽法輕重之議。其始，鹽入歲才四十萬緡，末乃至六百萬緡，幾當天下賦稅之半。暨大曆末，公私充羡，軍國資運濟之需，其利蓋盛布矣。今晏事詳於本傳，要其術而酌參之，非司鹺者所當心乎？
頃者計臣列疏，皇上慨然興行，兩淮二浙之閒特設都御史，任整理鹽法之計，蓋百數十年不幾遺者也。然初法久失，計臣所陳之具多按舊故，其猶備失未修舉者，則亦司鹺之臣所當通變而議之也。夫今憲臣所整理之方，鹽利數十倍天下，古邊郡所全資其飛輓者。昔宋雍熙中，令商輸芻粟於塞，特優其直，倍給以江淮之鹽。支兵之計，宋迄賴之。故我
translation_en:
…abolish it. Only under Emperors Zhao and Xuan of the Han, following proposals by men of worth and ability, were the regulations for the monopoly on salt boiling intermittently suspended. Thus benefits reached those below, and the common people enjoyed respite. The monopoly was again abolished during Emperor Yuan’s Chuyuan era, but after a year [?] the salt offices were reestablished. These prohibitions have therefore persisted throughout the ages. Successive dynasties relaxed them only slightly, and government salt boiling and sale revived. Under the Tang, Liu Yan was appointed Salt and Iron Commissioner and submitted proposals concerning the regulation of the salt administration. At first, annual salt receipts amounted to only 400,000 strings of cash; eventually they reached 6,000,000 strings, nearly half the empire’s tax revenues. By the end of the Dali era, both public and private resources were abundant. The needs of the army and state for funding, transport, and relief were met, and the benefits were widely distributed. Liu Yan’s activities are described in detail in his biography. Should those responsible for salt administration not give thought to extracting the essentials of his methods and judiciously adapting them?
Recently, the officials responsible for state finance set out their proposals in memorials. His Majesty resolutely put them into effect, specially appointing a Censor-in-chief for the Lianghuai and Liangzhe regions and entrusting him with measures to put the salt administration in order. This was something scarcely attended to for more than a hundred years [?]. Yet the original regulations have long fallen into disuse, and the measures presented by the fiscal officials mostly follow established precedents. Whatever remains defective and has not been restored [?] likewise calls for deliberation and adaptation by the officials responsible for salt administration. As for the measures now being put in order by the censorial official, salt revenues are several tens of times those of the empire [?]; formerly, the frontier commanderies depended entirely on them for the rapid transport of supplies. During the Song’s Yongxi era, merchants were ordered to deliver fodder and grain to the frontier. They were offered especially favorable prices, receiving double compensation in salt from the Jianghuai region. The Song continued to rely on this method of provisioning its troops. Thus our…

title: 嘉靖三十一年應天府鄉試錄
text:
聖祖因立轉運提舉司而下令凡開中鹽糧所
司先論邊地米直貴賤及道路遠近險易
定則例奏聞出榜召商中納然則鹽法之
行邊儲之計莫先焉而部議乃不深求其
所濟何也夫大荒窮漠不推通變之法則
禾黍末獲於秋成粒米無狼戾之藉穀粟
稍歉於時詘田野有鼠稾之思兵之先苦
匱乏蓋職此矣寧不圖周其後哉今宜於
邊方立常平之司主以曹郎使總一鎮芻
===
粟之計屬以有司俾覘四方平踊之直而
憲臣首重邊儲并及鹽司之職掌治其正
課招商令赴中納之地括其餘鹽解邊分
貯常平之庫由是派開中之商各輸芻粟
於遠邊而附近之鎮官司自平其市糴則
邊儲庶其有濟乎故曰捐近以計遠國無
弗利矣非此其當務邪抑二政之修舉咸
要而難易則不能無閒矣蓋營田興於本
業積儲之餘作於人情悅趨之會誠得其
punctuated: 聖祖因立轉運提舉司，而下令：凡開中鹽糧，所司先論邊地米直貴賤及道路遠近險易，定則例奏聞，出榜召商中納。然則鹽法之行，邊儲之計莫先焉，而部議乃不深求其所濟，何也？夫大荒窮漠，不推通變之法，則禾黍末獲於秋成，粒米無狼戾之藉；穀粟稍歉於時詘，田野有鼠稾之思。兵之先苦匱乏，蓋職此矣，寧不圖周其後哉？今宜於邊方立常平之司，主以曹郎，使總一鎮芻粟之計，屬以有司，俾覘四方平踊之直。而憲臣首重邊儲，并及鹽司之職掌，治其正課，招商令赴中納之地，括其餘鹽，解邊分貯常平之庫。由是派開中之商，各輸芻粟於遠邊，而附近之鎮，官司自平其市糴，則邊儲庶其有濟乎？故曰：「捐近以計遠，國無弗利矣。」非此其當務邪？抑二政之修舉咸要，而難易則不能無閒矣。蓋營田興於本業積儲之餘，作於人情悅趨之會，誠得其
translation_en:
…our sagely founding emperor accordingly established Salt Transport Commissions and Salt Distribution Supervisories and issued this order: whenever grain deliveries were solicited in exchange for salt certificates, the responsible officials were first to assess grain prices at the frontier and the distance and difficulty of the routes, establish regulations and report them to the throne, and then post notices inviting merchants to make deliveries. Thus, in administering the salt system, nothing takes precedence over provisioning the frontier. Why, then, do the ministry’s deliberations fail to examine thoroughly how this purpose can be served? In the remote wilderness and farthest deserts, unless adaptable measures are implemented, grain and millet may fail to be harvested in autumn [?], leaving no abundance of grain upon which to draw. When grain supplies fall even slightly short in straitened times, people in the countryside think of grain left by rats [?]. This is precisely why the soldiers suffer shortages first. Should we not devise means to provide adequately for them thereafter?

Ever-normal granary offices should now be established along the frontier, each headed by a ministry bureau official and charged with overseeing the fodder and grain supplies of an entire frontier command. The local authorities should be placed under them and instructed to monitor prices throughout the surrounding regions, whether stable or rising. The censorial official should give first priority to frontier reserves while also attending to the responsibilities of the salt administration: managing its regular levy, recruiting merchants and directing them to the designated delivery points, and collecting the surplus salt for transport to the frontier and distribution among the ever-normal storehouses. Merchants participating in the grain-for-salt system would then be assigned to deliver fodder and grain to the distant frontier, while at the nearer commands the authorities themselves would stabilize prices for their grain purchases. Might this not help replenish frontier reserves? Thus it is said: “Forgo what is near to provide for what is distant, and the state will benefit in every respect.” Is this not the urgent task?

Yet implementing both these policies is essential, though they necessarily differ in difficulty. Agricultural colonies can be established when the fundamental occupation of farming has produced accumulated reserves, and undertaken when people are willing and eager to participate. If indeed the right…

title: 嘉靖三十一年應天府鄉試錄
text:
人振理之則壑闕有地非强民以所不欲
經費在官非括衆以所難致事權無分掣
之患則寛徭平征勸之旣易集功弊隙無
旁出之慮則計財程役施之自鮮敗事故
曰其難有閒也惟鹽政則非旦夕可議者
故非變而通之必不能以濟矣葢利之所
行巧遠則弊之所伏者衆法之所治者嚴
則姦之所匿者深勢要占討足以困官商
之守支而邊儲開中無樂應之人矣豪姦
===
禁鬻不先給竈戸之工本而塲丁煎貿無
寄脊之地矣常股存積額名互變以相欺
代支透派詭跡交隱而難究其最患者邊
壤處於小守而芻粟鮮羨故糴價歲不能
無貴屯田廢於不耕而餉餽益艱故軍儲
時不能無匱則鹽法之初政不易復其亦
勢所必至哉此承學所以有常平通變之
議也或曰二政興行何以塞管商功利之
譏無乃非今
punctuated:
人振理之，則壑闕有地，非强民以所不欲；經費在官，非括衆以所難致。事權無分掣之患，則寛徭平征，勸之旣易集功；弊隙無旁出之慮，則計財程役，施之自鮮敗事。故曰其難有閒也。惟鹽政則非旦夕可議者，故非變而通之，必不能以濟矣。葢利之所行巧遠，則弊之所伏者衆；法之所治者嚴，則姦之所匿者深。勢要占討，足以困官商之守支，而邊儲開中無樂應之人矣。豪姦禁鬻，不先給竈戸之工本，而塲丁煎貿無寄脊之地矣。常股存積，額名互變以相欺；代支透派，詭跡交隱而難究。其最患者，邊壤處於小守，而芻粟鮮羨，故糴價歲不能無貴；屯田廢於不耕，而餉餽益艱，故軍儲時不能無匱。則鹽法之初政不易復，其亦勢所必至哉！此承學所以有常平通變之議也。

或曰：「二政興行，何以塞管商功利之譏？無乃非今
translation_en:
…people to put it in order, then there is land available in the ravines and gaps [?]; this does not compel the people to do what they do not wish. The expenses are borne by the authorities; this does not squeeze the populace for what they can scarcely provide. If administrative authority suffers no divided control or obstruction, then lightening labor service and equalizing levies will encourage the people and readily yield results. If there is no fear of abuses arising through other openings, then calculating expenditure and apportioning labor will seldom lead to failure. Thus I say that the difficulties involved differ. Salt administration, however, is not something that can be settled overnight. Unless it is modified to meet circumstances, it certainly cannot bring relief.

Where profit extends through cunning and far afield [?], lurking abuses multiply; where laws impose stringent controls, wrongdoing conceals itself more deeply. The powerful and influential appropriate claims, leaving authorized salt merchants stranded as they await their allotments; consequently, no one willingly responds to the offer of salt certificates in exchange for provisioning frontier stores. Powerful malefactors restrict salt sales [?], failing first to provide salt-producing households with their working capital, so that workers at the saltworks have no footing [?] from which to boil and trade salt. Under the regular and reserve quotas, amounts and designations are interchanged to perpetrate fraud; substitute withdrawals and unauthorized allocations involve deceptive practices that conceal one another and are difficult to investigate. Most troubling is that the frontier is thinly defended [?] and has little surplus fodder or grain, so purchase prices inevitably rise from year to year. Military agricultural colonies fall into disuse through failure to cultivate them, and provisioning grows increasingly difficult, so military stores inevitably suffer periodic shortages. That the original arrangements of the salt system cannot easily be restored—is this not also an inevitable consequence of circumstances? This is why I, a student of received learning, have proposed adapting the ever-normal granary system to present needs.

Someone asks: “If these two policies are put into effect, how will you silence the criticism that they pursue achievement and profit in the manner of Guan Zhong and Shang Yang? Might they be inappropriate for the present …

title: 嘉靖三十一年應天府鄉試錄
text:
聖世所當講邪夫蚩尤作五虐之法唐虞用之
而不改重黎辨九野之序夏商因之而不
廢苟以帝王公利天下之心行二子與時
相推之道孰謂其非王政邪故文帝好黃
老猶比賢商之成康孔明慕管樂乃亦庶
幾三代之伊呂夫二政誠修明令安攘
外之業有振焉則五三聖人復起知必從
之而不變矣
第五問
===
同考試官教諭盧　批〔援引〕
國家舊政歷歷指諸掌且能深明今日
朝謨之所急而采陳之以忠悃得士如此可遂也已宜錄
考試官修撰郭　批〔條陳安攘要務皆鑿鑿可〕
行予非六事而有武備者耶可以占其用矣
考試官右中允尹　批〔書生而能熟〕
國朝之政悉邊陲之務斯已難矣况其志之忠邪取之
中國之馭戎狄其勝之也必以氣而其制
punctuated:
聖世所當講邪？夫蚩尤作五虐之法，唐虞用之而不改；重黎辨九野之序，夏商因之而不廢。苟以帝王公利天下之心，行二子與時相推之道，孰謂其非王政邪？故文帝好黃老，猶比賢商之成康；孔明慕管樂，乃亦庶幾三代之伊呂。夫二政誠修明，令安攘外之業有振焉，則五三聖人復起，知必從之而不變矣。
第五問
同考試官教諭盧，批〔援引〕國家舊政，歷歷指諸掌，且能深明今日朝謨之所急，而采陳之以忠悃。得士如此，可遂也已，宜錄。
考試官修撰郭，批〔條陳安攘要務，皆鑿鑿可〕行。予非六事而有武備者耶？可以占其用矣。
考試官右中允尹，批〔書生而能熟〕國朝之政，悉邊陲之務，斯已難矣，况其志之忠邪？取之。
中國之馭戎狄，其勝之也必以氣，而其制
translation_en:
…appropriate for discussion in the present sage-governed age? Chiyou devised the laws of the five cruel punishments, yet Tang and Yu employed them without alteration; Chong and Li distinguished the ordering of the nine regions, and the Xia and Shang followed it without abandoning it. If, with the impartial concern of the sage emperors and kings for benefiting all under Heaven, one implements the methods by which those two men [Guan Zhong and Shang Yang] adapted to their times, who could say that this is not kingly government? Thus Emperor Wen favored the teachings of Huangdi and Laozi, yet was still compared in worth to “Cheng and Kang of Shang” [?]; Kongming admired Guan Zhong and Yue Yi, yet likewise approached the stature of Yi Yin and Lü Shang of the Three Dynasties. If these two policies are truly put into good order, so that the work of securing peace and repelling external enemies is reinvigorated [?], then, were the sages—the Five Emperors and Three Kings—to arise again, we may be certain that they would follow them without alteration.
Fifth Question
Associate Examiner Lu, Instructor, comments: 〔Citing〕 the dynasty’s former policies, he sets them out as clearly as if pointing to his own palm. Moreover, he thoroughly understands the urgent priorities of present court deliberations and selects and presents them with loyal sincerity. With a man of this quality obtained, our purpose may be fulfilled. He should be selected.
Examiner Guo, Senior Compiler, comments: 〔He sets out the essential tasks of securing peace and repelling external enemies, all of them demonstrably practicable.〕 “Am I not one who includes military preparedness among the six matters?” [?] From this one can judge his usefulness.
Examiner Yin, Right Companion of the Heir Apparent, comments: 〔For a scholar to be familiar with〕 the policies of our dynasty and thoroughly understand frontier affairs is already difficult. How much more commendable, then, is the loyalty of his purpose! Select him.
In China’s management of the Rong and Di, victory over them necessarily depends on fighting spirit, while bringing them under control…

title: 嘉靖三十一年應天府鄉試錄
text:
之也必以計氣惰而不作則功無可振矣
計忽而不懲則備無可持矣功不振難與
言戰備不持難與言守戰守先無所待欲
戎狄之爲我馭也不旣左乎夫惰氣久積
軍士無勇之效也忽計相循將臣不察之
過也虜患莫之過靖其此之繇邪執事策
承學以方
今禦虜大務愚非能知之然私嘗槪於中矣
請先明作氣之說因條近計之不可忽者
試詳擇焉夫戎狄之人生於窮漠之壤長
===
於盛陰之地食肉飲酪故饑寒罷苦不能
侵衣毛寢皮故風雨霜露不能害習搏射
便馳騁以輕生好戰去來鳥舉難得而制
也然廬帳各私則必興擁護之念財畜相
後則多積顧戀之志其貪暴不忍棄者豈
與華人之情獨異哉惟中國畏其勇悍不
敢與相校也故彼得挾所能以相恐動而
豪健敢果之氣因索然莫自奮蘇矣竈鏬
punctuated:
之也必以計。氣惰而不作，則功無可振矣；計忽而不懲，則備無可持矣。功不振，難與言戰；備不持，難與言守。戰守先無所待，欲戎狄之爲我馭也，不旣左乎？夫惰氣久積，軍士無勇之效也；忽計相循，將臣不察之過也。虜患莫之過靖，其此之繇邪？執事策承學以方今禦虜大務，愚非能知之，然私嘗槪於中矣。請先明作氣之說，因條近計之不可忽者，試詳擇焉。
夫戎狄之人，生於窮漠之壤，長於盛陰之地。食肉飲酪，故饑寒罷苦不能侵；衣毛寢皮，故風雨霜露不能害。習搏射，便馳騁，以輕生好戰，去來鳥舉，難得而制也。然廬帳各私，則必興擁護之念；財畜相後，則多積顧戀之志。其貪暴不忍棄者，豈與華人之情獨異哉？惟中國畏其勇悍，不敢與相校也，故彼得挾所能以相恐動，而豪健敢果之氣因索然莫自奮蘇矣。竈鏬
translation_en:
…controlling them must depend on planning. If martial spirit grows listless and is not roused, military achievement cannot be revived; if planning is neglected and the fault goes uncorrected, defensive preparations cannot be maintained. Without renewed military achievement, it is difficult to speak of fighting; without sustained preparations, it is difficult to speak of defense. When neither fighting nor defense has anything to rely upon from the outset, is it not misguided to expect the Rong and Di to submit to our control? Long-accumulated lethargy results from the soldiers’ lack of courage; persistent neglect of planning is the fault of commanders who fail to exercise scrutiny. The threat from the northern invaders remains unpacified [?]: might this be its cause? You gentlemen have questioned us students on the great tasks of resisting the invaders at present. Ignorant as I am, I cannot claim to understand them, yet privately I have often felt deeply troubled about them. Allow me first to explain how martial spirit may be roused, and then to enumerate the immediate measures that must not be neglected, for your careful consideration and selection.
The Rong and Di are born in the remote desert and grow up in lands of intense cold. They eat meat and drink fermented milk, so hunger, cold, exhaustion, and hardship cannot wear them down; they wear fur and sleep on hides, so wind, rain, frost, and dew cannot harm them. Practiced in fighting and archery, adept at riding at speed, they hold life cheap and delight in warfare. They come and go like birds taking flight, making them difficult to bring under control. Yet because each has his own dwelling and tent, each must feel a desire to protect them; with wealth and livestock left behind [?], they harbor many attachments and concerns. In what these rapacious and violent people cannot bear to abandon, how could their feelings differ from those of the Chinese? It is simply that China fears their courage and ferocity and dares not pit itself against them. Thus they can use their abilities to intimidate us, while our own bold, vigorous, and resolute spirit consequently withers, unable to revive itself. Zao Xia [?] …

title: 嘉靖三十一年應天府鄉試錄
text:
之言曰戰勝之威民氣百倍敗兵之卒沒
世不復此言氣之勇怯在所作之殊成也
昔秦據關中地制諸侯可謂九不當一然
秦人能用賞罰信其民使樂趨公戰作其
挺鬬不折之氣故旣併天下猶出餘威逐
能卻匈奴七百里外俾所收地爲郡縣其
人卒無敢彎弓一報怨者漢自白登之役
文景亦不欲勞民鋒鏑至輸繒結婚不悔武
帝赫然怒絕之任用衛霍諸將施兵二十
===
年不休觧當是時漢人視踐胡中如行市
肆墟里間尚以其人爲足畏也哉故闢疆
萬里空漠南之王庭焉夫秦之作民也以
信法漢之厲士也以任將法信而民敢死
將任而士效功此氣之所以奮振不衰也
今天下法弊於因循故人皆以寇爲玩將
習於貪懦故法削不可以繩下陵夷相媮
是安得氣之作厲而無惰乎夫愚〔竊謂近〕
計之不可忽者蓋譫我
punctuated:
之言曰：「戰勝之威，民氣百倍；敗兵之卒，沒世不復。」此言氣之勇怯，在所作之殊成也。昔秦據關中地制諸侯，可謂九不當一。然秦人能用賞罰信其民，使樂趨公戰，作其挺鬬不折之氣，故旣併天下，猶出餘威，逐能卻匈奴七百里外，俾所收地爲郡縣，其人卒無敢彎弓一報怨者。漢自白登之役，文景亦不欲勞民鋒鏑，至輸繒結婚不悔。武帝赫然怒絕之，任用衛霍諸將，施兵二十年不休觧。當是時，漢人視踐胡中，如行市肆墟里間，尚以其人爲足畏也哉？故闢疆萬里，空漠南之王庭焉。夫秦之作民也以信法，漢之厲士也以任將。法信而民敢死，將任而士效功，此氣之所以奮振不衰也。
今天下法弊於因循，故人皆以寇爲玩；將習於貪懦，故法削不可以繩下。陵夷相媮，是安得氣之作厲而無惰乎？夫愚〔竊謂近〕計之不可忽者，蓋譫我
translation_en:
…said: “With the prestige of victory in battle, the people's spirit increases a hundredfold; the soldiers of a defeated army never recover for the rest of their lives.” This means that courage and timidity depend on the differing results of efforts to arouse morale [?]. Formerly, Qin occupied Guanzhong and used its position to control the feudal lords: one might say that nine could not match one. Yet the men of Qin could employ rewards and punishments to win their people's trust, making them eager to fight for the state and arousing an unyielding spirit of combat. Thus, even after unifying All Under Heaven, Qin still deployed its remaining might and was able [?] to drive the Xiongnu back more than seven hundred li, turning the recovered territory into commanderies and counties. In the end, none of those people dared draw a bow even once to avenge their grievances. After the encounter at Baideng, the Han emperors Wen and Jing likewise wished to spare their people the toil of warfare; they went so far as to send silk and establish marriage alliances, without regret. Emperor Wu, in great anger, broke off relations with them, appointed Wei, Huo, and other generals, and waged war for twenty years without respite. At that time, the men of Han regarded treading through Hu territory as no different from walking among market stalls and village lanes. Could they still have considered those people worth fearing? Thus they extended the frontier ten thousand li and emptied the royal court south of the desert. Qin aroused its people through dependable laws; Han encouraged its soldiers by entrusting its generals with command. When laws were dependable, the people dared to die; when generals were entrusted with command, soldiers rendered meritorious service. This is why their spirit rose vigorously and did not decline.
Today, throughout the realm, the laws have been undermined by habitual inaction, so everyone treats the raiders lightly. Generals have become accustomed to greed and cowardice, so discipline has weakened and cannot restrain their subordinates. As decline continues, they encourage one another in laxity. How, then, can their spirit be aroused and sharpened, without indolence? As for my humble view, 〔I venture to say that immediate〕 plans must not be neglected; indeed, [the text is unclear: “speaking deliriously of our…”] [?] …

title: 嘉靖三十一年應天府鄉試錄
text:
高皇帝訓言有以推知之也在昔
皇祖出入百戰威行乎殊俗元君昇遯朔漠播
竄據其全遺萬世可以蒙安矣然
訓垂久後猶拳拳於胡戎密邇之患言必選將
練兵時謹備之思患豫防不因其積衰稍
懈此
文皇帝所以躬擐戎胄三窮沙磧之師而不厭
者也今我
皇上虛心獨斷銳志釐革修舉大政期盛撻伐
之威臣民孰不願佐
===
下風者顧時視
二祖不能無少異而患深百年非一旦夕可袪
制焉苟任事者不先圖所恃備徒務為應
文塞具苟幾目前之無患則
國家大計誰與終持之乎愚請繹
祖訓之深意不敢久遠喻顧借
先朝為喻夫訓所謂選將者往正統以前各
邊將臣大抵多推挍於老成勳舊之中被
punctuated: 高皇帝訓言，有以推知之也。在昔，皇祖出入百戰，威行乎殊俗，元君昇遯朔漠，播竄據其全遺，萬世可以蒙安矣。然訓垂久後，猶拳拳於胡戎密邇之患，言必選將練兵，時謹備之。思患豫防，不因其積衰稍懈，此文皇帝所以躬擐戎胄，三窮沙磧之師而不厭者也。今我皇上虛心獨斷，銳志釐革，修舉大政，期盛撻伐之威，臣民孰不願佐下風者？顧時視二祖，不能無少異，而患深百年，非一旦夕可袪制焉。苟任事者不先圖所恃備，徒務為應文塞具，苟幾目前之無患，則國家大計，誰與終持之乎？愚請繹祖訓之深意，不敢久遠喻，顧借先朝為喻。夫訓所謂選將者，往正統以前，各邊將臣大抵多推挍於老成勳舊之中，被
translation_en:
…the admonitions of Emperor Gao furnish grounds for understanding this. In former times, the imperial ancestor fought a hundred battles, and his might reached peoples of different customs. The Yuan ruler fled into the northern desert, wandering in exile and holding on to what remained intact of his domain [?]; peace might thus have been enjoyed for ten thousand generations. Yet in the instructions he bequeathed to distant posterity, he remained deeply concerned about the danger posed by the nearby northern peoples. He insisted that commanders be selected and troops trained, and that vigilant preparations be maintained at all times. He anticipated danger and guarded against it, never relaxing his vigilance merely because the enemy had long been declining. This is why Emperor Wen personally donned armor and helmet and tirelessly led three campaigns into the farthest sandy wastes.

Now our sovereign, receptive to counsel yet deciding for himself, is firmly resolved upon reform. He is restoring the great affairs of government, seeking to display the full might of punitive expeditions. What subject, official or commoner, would not wish to lend his humble assistance? Yet present circumstances cannot be entirely the same as those of the two imperial ancestors. The trouble has deepened over a hundred years and cannot be dispelled and brought under control in a single day or night. If those charged with affairs do not first plan the preparations on which they must rely, but merely attend to paperwork and perfunctory formalities [?], hoping only to escape trouble for the moment, who will sustain the state's great plans to their completion?

I venture to ask leave to expound the profound meaning of the Ancestral Instructions. I dare not draw examples from the distant past, but will instead use earlier reigns of our dynasty. As for what the Instructions call selecting commanders: before the Zhengtong reign, the military commanders on the various frontiers were, for the most part, selected from among seasoned veterans and longstanding men of merit [?], receiving…

title: 嘉靖三十一年應天府鄉試錄
text:
惟勞績久著夷虜素憚其威名故動獲成
功然永樂時
成祖猶歎恨淇國公丘福之僨事故弘治火篩
之犯本兵馬端肅慨然思邊師不稱欲起
舊將於老廢令佐軍事之語謗也今中外
將領孰爲老成耆宿可倚於衛敵愾作三
軍未振之氣夷虜憚慴動而能成功耶此
選將之不可忽者其計在本兵也所謂練
兵者往時京衛諸兵
===
祖宗特設大營團練之歲久而弊易之以三營
又歲久而弊易之以十二營焉夫正統景
泰之間京兵遭逆虜戕傷尺籍大耗缺矣
大臣議宜修政變其竊寇而振揚之時則
將有死綏之志士有超距之能故虜偵其
難間則悍計日沮阻也玆我
皇上痛創內監提督之弊作新京營將兵之制
戎政開府設總督協理之官
神樞改營增招募收補之籍
punctuated:
惟勞績久著，夷虜素憚其威名，故動獲成功。然永樂時，成祖猶歎恨淇國公丘福之僨事。故弘治火篩之犯，本兵馬端肅慨然思邊師不稱，欲起舊將於老廢，令佐軍事之語謗也。今中外將領，孰爲老成耆宿，可倚於衛敵愾，作三軍未振之氣，夷虜憚慴，動而能成功耶？此選將之不可忽者，其計在本兵也。
所謂練兵者，往時京衛諸兵，祖宗特設大營團練之。歲久而弊，易之以三營；又歲久而弊，易之以十二營焉。夫正統、景泰之間，京兵遭逆虜戕傷，尺籍大耗缺矣。大臣議宜修政，變其竊寇而振揚之。時則將有死綏之志，士有超距之能，故虜偵其難間，則悍計日沮阻也。玆我皇上痛創內監提督之弊，作新京營將兵之制，戎政開府，設總督、協理之官；神樞改營，增招募收補之籍。
translation_en:
…Their meritorious service had long been distinguished, and the foreign foes had always feared their martial reputation; hence, whenever they acted, they achieved success. Yet even in the Yongle reign, Chengzu lamented the disastrous failure of Qiu Fu, Duke of Qi. Thus, when Huoshai invaded during the Hongzhi reign, Ma Duansu, the Minister of War, deeply deplored the inadequacy of the frontier forces and wished to recall veteran commanders who had been retired on account of age, to assist with military affairs; the wording concerning criticism here is doubtful [?]. Among commanders in the capital and the provinces today, who are the seasoned veterans upon whom we can rely to defend against the enemy and inspire martial resolve [?], rouse the still-unawakened spirit of the armies, strike fear into foreign foes, and achieve success whenever they act? This is why the selection of commanders must not be neglected; responsibility for planning it rests with the Minister of War.
As for what is called training troops, formerly our imperial ancestors specially established large camps to assemble and train the soldiers of the capital guards. When abuses developed over time, these were replaced with the Three Camps; when abuses again developed over time, these were replaced with the Twelve Camps. During the Zhengtong and Jingtai reigns, the capital troops suffered slaughter at the hands of the rebellious foe, and their muster rolls were severely depleted. The high ministers proposed reforming military administration, transforming their condition of ‘furtive banditry’ [?], and reinvigorating them. At that time, commanders were resolved to die rather than retreat, and soldiers possessed the agility to leap obstacles. Consequently, when the enemy's scouts discovered how difficult it was to exploit an opening, their aggressive designs met with increasing frustration.
Now our emperor, deeply troubled by the abuses of eunuch supervision, has renewed the system governing the commanders and soldiers of the capital camps. An office for military administration has been established, with posts of Supreme Commander and Associate Administrator; the Divine Pivot Camp (Shenshu) has been reorganized, and its rolls augmented through recruitment and the enrollment of replacements…

title: 嘉靖三十一年應天府鄉試錄
text:
矣紛紛議推用邊將調邊丁以教內士欲其
日閑於技擊也今訓練二年不聞少效尺
寸顧徒稱京兵難用議調邊鎮易其久惰
弱也夫以此驕慣之衆置之孤危之鎮聚
㐌則仰食縣官民不勝其擾徙遷則煩
費邊儲國不堪其耗□知□京兵不能制其
㐲氣出塞獨可得其戰力哉然昔人稱幽
燕之民沉鷙多材力今之京兵他不能蕩豈
今之
===
京兵獨非其邪而何其不能強也此練兵之不
可忽者其計在諸將也所謂謹備者自古
中國守四夷必因徼險爲限塞繕亭堠嚴
烽燧歷世所不能廢而邊臣苟且易視之今
宣大邊垣虜詭以易馬盡敢墮薊州所修
築者逾二年弗克究功虜脫肆孽若上歲
即何賴以搤制乎其不可忽者一也天下
之勢若提衡平者欲重內以制外一遇警
變不得不重外也往也先之變
punctuated:
矣。紛紛議推用邊將、調邊丁以教內士，欲其日閑於技擊也。今訓練二年，不聞少效尺寸，顧徒稱京兵難用，議調邊鎮，易其久惰弱也。夫以此驕慣之衆，置之孤危之鎮，聚㐌則仰食縣官，民不勝其擾；徙遷則煩費邊儲，國不堪其耗。□知□京兵不能制其㐲氣，出塞獨可得其戰力哉？然昔人稱幽燕之民沉鷙多材力，今之京兵他不能蕩，豈今之京兵獨非其邪？而何其不能強也？此練兵之不可忽者，其計在諸將也。
所謂謹備者，自古中國守四夷，必因徼險爲限塞，繕亭堠，嚴烽燧，歷世所不能廢，而邊臣苟且易視之。今宣大邊垣，虜詭以易馬，盡敢墮；薊州所修築者，逾二年弗克究功。虜脫肆孽若上歲，即何賴以搤制乎？其不可忽者一也。天下之勢若提衡，平者欲重內以制外，一遇警變，不得不重外也。往也先之變，
translation_en:
…Such changes have been made. Proposals abound to employ frontier commanders and transfer frontier soldiers to instruct the troops at the capital, so that they may become increasingly practiced in combat skills. Yet after two years of training, we hear of not the slightest success. Instead, people merely declare that the capital troops are difficult to employ and propose transferring them to frontier garrisons to remedy their longstanding indolence and weakness. But if these pampered troops are stationed at isolated, endangered garrisons, when concentrated there they will depend upon government provisions, and the people will find their disturbances unbearable; when moved, they will consume frontier stores at great expense, and the state will find the drain intolerable. [Illegible text] If the capital troops cannot have their unruly spirit subdued [?], can sending them beyond the passes alone bring out their fighting strength? Yet people of old described the inhabitants of You and Yan as steady, fierce, and endowed with talent and strength. The capital troops of today cannot sweep away [the enemy?] [?]. Surely these capital troops are themselves drawn from those same people? Why, then, can they not be made strong? This is why training troops must not be neglected; the planning rests with the commanders.
As for exercising care in defensive preparations: since antiquity, when the Central Kingdom defended itself against the peoples of the four quarters, it invariably used difficult terrain along its frontiers to establish defensive boundaries, repaired watchposts, and maintained strict vigilance at beacon stations. Successive ages could never dispense with these measures, yet frontier officials treat them carelessly and lightly. Now, along the frontier walls of Xuanfu and Datong, the enemy has used horse trading as a pretext and dared to demolish them all [?]; the construction undertaken at Jizhou remains unfinished after more than two years. If the enemy should unleash destruction as it did last year, what could we rely upon to check it? This is one matter that must not be neglected. The strategic disposition of the realm resembles holding up a balance: in ordinary times, one seeks to give weight to the interior in order to control the exterior, but once an emergency arises, one has no choice but to give weight to the exterior. Formerly, during the crisis involving Esen…

title: 嘉靖三十一年應天府鄉試錄
text:
京師震動大臣有奏留邊將衛內者葉文莊
疏議曰頃獨石馬營不棄六師何以憂土
木紫荆白羊不破虜騎何以伺都城夫守
邊鎮所以重京師也後虜果覘外備之固
則內犯阻而悔罪歸命之使通矣夫
京兵即不習戰隸尺籍者尚十數萬衆苟訓
教有方其强猶反掌耳豈若諸鎮之單懸
弱卸與虜持抗者比哉於其精銳不顧邊
守之難固門戶弗禦堂室能晏然乎其不
可忽者二也互市之法自古鮮以施之北
===
狄正統中也先因
先朝歸附僞求互市通
貢盡窺中國之虛實是以盜邊其邪心乃後
復詐請和邊臣奏欲假和以緩之也本兵
駁議曰虜方以和詐我許之可得其緩邪
夫互市之請即虜也先之遺詐也羈縻之
說即邊臣許和緩師之逸計也利害往迹
昭然著明而可久蹈之乎其不可忽者三
punctuated:
京師震動，大臣有奏留邊將衛內者。葉文莊疏議曰：「頃獨石、馬營不棄，六師何以憂土木？紫荆、白羊不破，虜騎何以伺都城？夫守邊鎮，所以重京師也。」後虜果覘外備之固，則內犯阻，而悔罪歸命之使通矣。夫京兵即不習戰，隸尺籍者尚十數萬衆，苟訓教有方，其强猶反掌耳。豈若諸鎮之單懸弱卸，與虜持抗者比哉？於其精銳，不顧邊守之難，固門戶弗禦，堂室能晏然乎？其不可忽者二也。
互市之法，自古鮮以施之北狄。正統中，也先因先朝歸附，僞求互市通貢，盡窺中國之虛實，是以盜邊。其邪心乃後復詐請和，邊臣奏欲假和以緩之也。本兵駁議曰：「虜方以和詐我，許之可得其緩邪？」夫互市之請，即虜也先之遺詐也；羈縻之說，即邊臣許和緩師之逸計也。利害往迹，昭然著明，而可久蹈之乎？其不可忽者三
translation_en:
…the capital was shaken, and some senior ministers memorialized requesting that frontier commanders be retained to defend the interior. Ye Wenzhuang argued in a memorial: “Had Dushi and Maying not recently been abandoned, how would the imperial armies have suffered disaster at Tumu? Had Zijing and Baiyang not been breached, how could the enemy cavalry have watched for an opportunity to attack the capital? Defending the frontier garrisons is precisely how one strengthens the capital.” Later, when the enemy indeed observed the strength of the outer defenses, their incursions into the interior were blocked, and envoys expressing repentance and offering submission began to arrive. Even if the capital troops are unpracticed in warfare, those on the military rolls still number over a hundred thousand. Provided they are properly trained, making them strong would be as easy as turning over one’s hand. How can their circumstances compare with those of the isolated frontier garrisons, weakly defended [?], which must contend directly with the enemy? As for their elite troops [?], to disregard the difficulty of defending the frontier—surely, if the gates are left undefended, can the inner chambers remain secure? This is the second matter that must not be neglected.
Since antiquity, the practice of mutual trade has seldom been extended to the northern peoples. During the Zhengtong reign, Yexian, taking advantage of submission under a preceding reign, deceitfully sought mutual trade and the exchange of tribute missions. He thoroughly reconnoitered China’s strengths and weaknesses and used this knowledge to raid the frontier. With the same malicious intent, he later again deceitfully requested peace. Frontier officials memorialized proposing to use peace negotiations to delay him. The Minister of War rebutted this proposal: “The enemy is now using peace to deceive us. Can accepting it really make him suspend his attacks?” Requests for mutual trade are precisely the deceit bequeathed by the enemy leader Yexian. Proposals for loose rein management are precisely the expedient schemes of frontier officials who would accept peace to postpone military action. The precedents showing their benefits and harms are manifestly clear. Can we continue to tread the same path? This is the third matter that must not be neglected…

title: 嘉靖三十一年應天府鄉試錄
text:
也
國家鹽政既不興修諸邊餽饟益乏是
故糴運不給至輦
京儲佐之然率一鍾不能致一石今調集益
廣邊餉益不可支然而其甚亟者持也夫招
勸土兵之令人知其爲而鎭臣莫能自信
則軍需空於調集之廣耳其不可忽者四
也大三衛屬夷我
祖宗所建樹爲東北屛蔽者彼其叛服弗常而
===
數端我之恩德狡險成性而間從虜之向
導此夷性難馴之固然使撫馭不失我能
潛奪其心則安知彼不效忠若往時乎聞
諸道路之言
國家誠大舉兵東翦逮州北除及顏則虜絕
引誘禍可不制自息此固事之宜重者
宸慮深遠豈外議所可測邪然二部苟不有以
懷之則屛蔽闕撤非所以自扞况今旣爲
彼虜抄國威之欲使叛降則其端大可見
punctuated:
也。
國家鹽政既不興修，諸邊餽饟益乏，是故糴運不給，至輦京儲佐之。然率一鍾不能致一石。今調集益廣，邊餉益不可支，然而其甚亟者持也。夫招勸土兵之令，人知其爲，而鎭臣莫能自信，則軍需空於調集之廣耳。其不可忽者四也。
大三衛屬夷，我祖宗所建樹爲東北屛蔽者。彼其叛服弗常，而數端我之恩德，狡險成性，而間從虜之向導，此夷性難馴之固然。使撫馭不失，我能潛奪其心，則安知彼不效忠若往時乎？聞諸道路之言，國家誠大舉兵，東翦逮州，北除及顏，則虜絕引誘，禍可不制自息。此固事之宜重者，宸慮深遠，豈外議所可測邪？然二部苟不有以懷之，則屛蔽闕撤，非所以自扞。况今旣爲彼虜抄，國威之欲使叛降，則其端大可見
translation_en:
…This is so.
Since the state has failed to restore and improve the salt administration, provisions for the frontier regions have grown increasingly scarce. Grain purchases and transport therefore cannot meet requirements, and supplies have even had to be carted from the capital’s reserves to supplement them. Yet ordinarily, the expenditure of one zhong of grain cannot deliver even one shi. Troops are now being mobilized ever more widely, and frontier provisioning is increasingly unsustainable. Yet the most urgent task is to hold firm [?]. Everyone knows what the order to recruit and encourage local troops is intended to accomplish, but the regional commanders cannot act with confidence themselves. Military resources are thus merely exhausted by the widening mobilization. This is the fourth matter that must not be neglected.
The dependent tribes of the Three Guards, here called the “Da Three Guards” [?], were established by our imperial ancestors as a defensive screen in the northeast. They alternate unpredictably between rebellion and submission and repeatedly test our benevolence [?]. Treachery and cunning have become their nature, and they sometimes serve as guides for the northern enemy. Such is the inherent difficulty of taming these tribes. Yet if we manage and conciliate them properly and can quietly win their hearts, how can we know that they will not serve loyally as they once did? I have heard people saying that, if the state truly mobilized a great army to destroy Daizhou [?] in the east and eliminate Jiyan [?] in the north, the enemy would lose those who guide and entice them, and the trouble could subside of itself without further suppression. This is certainly a matter requiring grave consideration. His Majesty’s deliberations are profound and far-reaching: how could outside commentators fathom them? Nevertheless, unless some means is found to win over these two tribes, our defensive screen will be breached and dismantled; this is no way to protect ourselves. Moreover, now that they have already been raided by those northern enemies, and intimidated into rebellion and surrender [?], the signs of this are plainly visible…

title: 嘉靖三十一年應天府鄉試錄
text:
矣其不可忽者五也夫謹備五計之不可
忽在任事大臣深思而預謀之可也語曰
前事之不忘則後事之師也今不懲艾旣
往以力持天下之大計則非所以爲
國家起福無形銷患未萌者矣夫鬼方必克
高宗所以盛中興之業玁狁于襄方叔所
以著古壯之猷振古殊績是安得不在
今日極盛之世邪是故誠思選將之爲要則
擇之不可不精求之不可不豫蓄之不可
===
不廣也夫節鉞所授必推天下之傑才事
權所與必協天下之夫論則擇之精矣明
立薦舉作養之法而不需於方急之時博
詢智謀男略之士而不拘於所出之塗則
求之能豫蓄之能廣矣由是風聲所招徠
意氣所感召得無如古名將者流應類以
出也乎思練兵之爲急則制之不可無紀
教之不可無法倡之不可無人也夫法律
嚴整所出無回亂之人營陣齊一所止無
punctuated: 矣。其不可忽者五也。夫謹備五計之不可忽，在任事大臣深思而預謀之可也。語曰：「前事之不忘，則後事之師也。」今不懲艾旣往，以力持天下之大計，則非所以爲國家起福無形、銷患未萌者矣。夫鬼方必克，高宗所以盛中興之業；玁狁于襄，方叔所以著古壯之猷。振古殊績，是安得不在今日極盛之世邪？是故誠思選將之爲要，則擇之不可不精，求之不可不豫，蓄之不可不廣也。夫節鉞所授，必推天下之傑才；事權所與，必協天下之夫論，則擇之精矣。明立薦舉作養之法，而不需於方急之時；博詢智謀男略之士，而不拘於所出之塗，則求之能豫，蓄之能廣矣。由是風聲所招徠，意氣所感召，得無如古名將者流應類以出也乎？思練兵之爲急，則制之不可無紀，教之不可無法，倡之不可無人也。夫法律嚴整，所出無回亂之人；營陣齊一，所止無
translation_en:
…This is the fifth matter that must not be neglected. As for attending carefully to these five indispensable measures, the great ministers charged with affairs should ponder them deeply and plan for them beforehand. As the saying goes, “Past events, if not forgotten, become teachers for what follows.” If we now fail to take warning from what has happened and firmly uphold the grand plans for the realm, we shall fail to bring blessings to the state before they take visible form or dispel troubles before they sprout. By conquering Guifang, Gaozong brought his work of dynastic restoration to greatness; by driving off the Xianyun, Fang Shu displayed his vigorous strategy even in old age [?]. Why should such extraordinary achievements of antiquity not also occur in this age of supreme flourishing?

Thus, if we truly recognize the importance of selecting commanders, we must choose them with discernment, seek them in advance, and maintain a broad pool of talent. Those granted the tally and battle-axe of command must be outstanding talents of the realm; those entrusted with authority over affairs must accord with the realm’s general judgment [?]. Then selection will be discerning. Clearly establish methods for recommending and nurturing talent, without waiting until an emergency arises; seek widely for men of intelligence and strategic ability [?], without restricting the paths by which they come forward. Then talent can be sought in advance and gathered in abundance. Attracted by the reputation of this endeavor and inspired by its spirit, would men like the famous commanders of antiquity not emerge in response, each answering the call of his kind?

If we recognize the urgency of training troops, their organization must have discipline, their instruction must have methods, and their leadership must have suitable men. When military regulations are strict and orderly, there will be no wayward or disorderly men among those who march out; when camps and formations are uniformly ordered, wherever they halt there will be no…

title: 嘉靖三十一年應天府鄉試錄
text:
驚擾之衆則制之有紀矣訓練於無事坐
作擊刺之咸宜毆率於有警摧鋒陷敵之
爭先則教之成其法倡之多其人矣由是
無攻而不取莫守而不固凡古名將所建
立者何嫌而不如志哉恩譬謹備之必時而
往怠之當懲也則修築之功雖勞民然所
以節時使之力施悅勸之道不可曲爲之
處乎互市之求雖禁行然所以通間諜之
要致招誘之方不可詔爲之謀乎鎮兵精
===
銳可挑矣然勢非斷急
京將不得假內衛之名以奪邊臣之所恃京
儲輦運可應矣然地本屯種軍士不得因
抄寇之擾以棄邊實之所資至若三衛屬
夷之經略則存乎遼薊鎮臣之籌策耳夫
撫之以恩潛消其攜貳之隙懾之以威陰
制其回易之姦精神折之於先不以一朝
細故忘
祖宗百年之深慮丈台精之於後不以一二人
punctuated: 驚擾之衆，則制之有紀矣。訓練於無事，坐作擊刺之咸宜；毆率於有警，摧鋒陷敵之爭先，則教之成其法，倡之多其人矣。由是無攻而不取，莫守而不固，凡古名將所建立者，何嫌而不如志哉？恩譬謹備之必時，而往怠之當懲也，則修築之功雖勞民，然所以節時使之力、施悅勸之道，不可曲爲之處乎？互市之求雖禁行，然所以通間諜之要、致招誘之方，不可詔爲之謀乎？鎮兵精銳可挑矣，然勢非斷急，京將不得假內衛之名，以奪邊臣之所恃。京儲輦運可應矣，然地本屯種，軍士不得因抄寇之擾，以棄邊實之所資。至若三衛屬夷之經略，則存乎遼薊鎮臣之籌策耳。夫撫之以恩，潛消其攜貳之隙；懾之以威，陰制其回易之姦。精神折之於先，不以一朝細故忘祖宗百年之深慮；丈台精之於後，不以一二人
translation_en:
…no troops are thrown into alarm or disorder where they halt: then their control is disciplined. Train them in uneventful times so that sitting, rising, striking, and thrusting are all properly performed; lead them when an alarm arises so that they vie to be first to break the enemy’s vanguard and penetrate his ranks. Then instruction will have established its methods, and leadership will have brought forth many capable men. Thus no attack will fail to take its objective, and no defense will lack firmness. As for all that famous generals of antiquity accomplished, what impediment could prevent us from fulfilling our aims?

[?] Vigilant preparation must be timely, and past negligence must be chastised. Although building and repairing fortifications burdens the people, could we not make careful arrangements to employ their labor at appropriate seasons and use means that encourage willing service? Although requests for mutual trade are prohibited, could we not devise plans [?] for the essential work of communicating through spies and for methods of attracting and winning people over?

Elite troops from the frontier garrisons may be selected, but unless circumstances are truly urgent [?], commanders in the capital must not invoke the needs of the inner guard to deprive frontier officials of the forces on which they rely. Supplies stored in the capital may be transported to meet needs, but the frontier land is fundamentally intended for military farming: soldiers must not abandon the resources that sustain the frontier because of disturbances caused by raiders.

As for managing the subject non-Han peoples of the Three Guards, this rests with the strategic planning of the garrison officials of Liao and Ji. Soothe them with kindness, quietly removing opportunities for estrangement and divided allegiance; overawe them with power, discreetly restraining their treachery in changing sides. Subdue them beforehand through spiritual resolve [?], and do not let a single day’s petty incident cause us to forget the imperial ancestors’ profound, century-long deliberations. Thereafter, refine [?] … and do not, on account of one or two men…

title: 嘉靖三十一年應天府鄉試錄
text:
阻化累醜類千百輩之死命則所謂屈戰
奪心善之善者在是矣雖然此固不足呫
呫道也要之在將得其人耳聞之論將品
者矣有一軍之將攻堅破強所向無前者
是也然可爲偏校之良而非邦國之寄有
一國之將出奇制勝所應不窮者是也然
可爲裨翼之特而非社稷之鎮夫惟天下
之將知有國而不知有家知有君而不
知有其身福於已而禍於人則功寧有所
不立利於今而害於後則事寧有所不成
此則古名世之傑所以垂勳業於久遠流
聲實於不窮者也以今
===
大聖人睿謨尤物側席勤求必得無若而人者
出仰副
宵旰之虛佇邪是惡寡聞不足備對幸執事
之財擇焉
punctuated: 阻化累醜類千百輩之死命，則所謂屈戰奪心，善之善者在是矣。雖然，此固不足呫呫道也，要之在將得其人耳。聞之論將品者矣：有一軍之將，攻堅破強，所向無前者是也；然可爲偏校之良，而非邦國之寄。有一國之將，出奇制勝，所應不窮者是也；然可爲裨翼之特，而非社稷之鎮。夫惟天下之將，知有國而不知有家，知有君而不知有其身；福於已而禍於人，則功寧有所不立；利於今而害於後，則事寧有所不成。此則古名世之傑所以垂勳業於久遠，流聲實於不窮者也。以今大聖人睿謨尤物，側席勤求，必得無若而人者出，仰副宵旰之虛佇邪？是惡寡聞，不足備對，幸執事之財擇焉。
translation_en:
…resistance to transformation imperil the lives of hundreds and thousands of their kind, then herein lies what is called subduing the enemy in battle and overcoming their resolve—the highest excellence of all. Even so, these matters hardly warrant tedious discussion. The essential point is simply to obtain the right men as commanders.

I have heard those who discuss the ranks of commanders say: there are commanders of a single army—men who assault strong positions and break powerful opponents, encountering no resistance wherever they advance. Yet such a man may be an excellent subordinate officer without being someone to whom the state can be entrusted. There are commanders of a single state—men who win through unexpected maneuvers and respond inexhaustibly to changing circumstances. Yet such a man may be an outstanding supporting officer without being a mainstay of the altars of soil and grain. Only a commander of all under Heaven knows that there is a state but gives no thought to his own household, and knows that there is a ruler but gives no thought to himself. If an achievement would benefit him but bring disaster upon others, he would rather leave it unaccomplished; if an undertaking would bring present advantage but cause future harm, he would rather leave it unfinished. It was through this that the renowned heroes of antiquity transmitted their meritorious achievements to distant generations and perpetuated both their reputations and their substantive accomplishments without end.

With our present great sage sovereign’s sagacious plans and exceptional gifts [?], and his earnest search for worthy men, sitting sideways on his seat in anxious anticipation, surely someone of this sort must emerge [?] to fulfill the expectant hopes of one who attends to government before dawn and late into the night? I am poorly informed [?], and cannot furnish an adequate reply. I hope that you, sir, will judge and select what is useful.

title: 嘉靖三十一年應天府鄉試錄
text:
應天府鄉試錄後序
嘉靖壬子秋八月當鄉試之
期應天府臣循
制具請
上以臣臺臣臣鏊充考試官欽承祇
役願得真才以副
明詔求賢致太平之意既取其雋
===
錄其文以
獻臣鏊謹序于後曰嘗稽古昔
帝王興道致治任賢以資化
理其取士之法不同而獲士
之報亦異唐虞至殷立賢無
方惟賢乂政盛莫可匹周之
盛時大司徒以鄉三物教萬
punctuated:
應天府鄉試錄後序

嘉靖壬子秋八月，當鄉試之期，應天府臣循制具請。上以臣臺臣臣鏊充考試官，欽承祇役，願得真才，以副明詔求賢致太平之意。既取其雋，錄其文以獻。臣鏊謹序于後曰：嘗稽古昔帝王興道致治，任賢以資化理。其取士之法不同，而獲士之報亦異。唐虞至殷，立賢無方，惟賢乂，政盛莫可匹。周之盛時，大司徒以鄉三物教萬
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination

In the eighth month of autumn in the renzi year of Jiajing [1552], when the Provincial Examination was due, the officials of Yingtian Prefecture submitted a formal request in accordance with established regulations. His Majesty appointed your servant Tai and your servant Ao [?] as Examiners. Reverently accepting this duty, we hoped to obtain men of true ability, fulfilling the intention of the enlightened edict to seek worthy men and bring about Great Peace. Having selected the outstanding candidates, we recorded their compositions for presentation to the throne. Your servant Ao respectfully appends this postface:

I have examined how the emperors and kings of antiquity promoted the Way and achieved good government, employing worthy men to assist in moral transformation and governance. Their methods of selecting scholars differed, and so too did the rewards they reaped from obtaining them. From the ages of Tang [Yao] and Yu [Shun] through the Yin dynasty, worthy men were appointed without restriction as to their origins. With the worthy alone governing, the excellence of their rule was beyond compare. At the height of the Zhou dynasty, the Minister of Education used the three categories of instruction in the districts to teach the myriad …

title: 嘉靖三十一年應天府鄉試錄
text:
民而賓興之鄉大夫三年大
比考其德行道藝而興賢者
能者鄉老及鄉大夫羣吏獻
賢能之書于王由是於變咸
寧之休文武成康卓矣萬世
頌之漢唐而下有明經賢良
孝廉博學宏詞茂才異等諸
科雖與上世制遠而因人立
法各有美意故議者謂二帝
===
三王之世多道德春秋戰國
之士多功利兩漢之士多才
節隋唐之士多辭藝風聲氣
習隨感而應建功立業故各
不同國上使然也洪惟我
punctuated: 民而賓興之。鄉大夫三年大比，考其德行道藝而興賢者能者，鄉老及鄉大夫羣吏獻賢能之書于王。由是於變咸寧之休，文武成康卓矣，萬世頌之。漢唐而下，有明經、賢良、孝廉、博學宏詞、茂才異等諸科，雖與上世制遠，而因人立法，各有美意。故議者謂二帝三王之世多道德，春秋戰國之士多功利，兩漢之士多才節，隋唐之士多辭藝。風聲氣習，隨感而應，建功立業，故各不同，國上使然也。洪惟我
translation_en: …the people, and honored the worthy as guests before recommending them for service. Every three years, the District Grand Masters conducted a major assessment, examining their virtuous conduct and their mastery of the Way and the arts, and recommending the worthy and able. The District Elders, together with the District Grand Masters and the assembled officials, presented the king with registers of the worthy and able. Thus arose the blessings of transformation and universal peace: the achievements of Kings Wen, Wu, Cheng, and Kang were outstanding, and all subsequent ages have praised them. From the Han and Tang onward, there were various categories of recruitment: Illuminating the Classics, Worthy and Good, Filial and Incorrupt, Broad Learning and Grand Literary Expression, Outstanding Talent of Exceptional Rank, and others. Although these were far removed from the institutions of high antiquity, each devised procedures suited to the people concerned and embodied commendable intentions. Hence commentators say that the age of the Two Emperors and Three Kings abounded in moral virtue; the scholars of the Spring and Autumn and Warring States periods emphasized achievement and advantage; those of the two Han dynasties, talent and integrity; and those of the Sui and Tang, literary skill. Prevailing influences and ingrained habits responded to what moved them; thus the achievements and undertakings of each age differed. Those at the head of the state made it so [?]. Reverently we consider our…

title: 嘉靖三十一年應天府鄉試錄
text:
祖宗稽古成治養士于學掄才以
科目而三載一興之
道本唐虞法鑒成周
章程品式至爲明備中間英俊
彙征彬彬蔚蔚得人之盛比
隆上世漢唐俱下風矣我
皇上光膺
===
天眷總覽萬機
憲
天法
祖
聖學日新
序禮和樂制作大備
中興文明之運寔甚煥乎士際
punctuated: 祖宗稽古成治，養士于學，掄才以科目，而三載一興之。道本唐虞，法鑒成周，章程品式至爲明備。中間英俊彙征，彬彬蔚蔚，得人之盛，比隆上世，漢唐俱下風矣。我皇上光膺天眷，總覽萬機，憲天法祖，聖學日新，序禮和樂，制作大備。中興文明之運，寔甚煥乎！士際
translation_en:
…our imperial ancestors examined antiquity to establish good government, nurtured scholars in the schools, and selected talent through the examination system, holding examinations once every three years. Their Way was rooted in Tang and Yu, and their institutions took the perfected Zhou as their model; their regulations and prescribed forms were exceptionally clear and comprehensive. Throughout this time, outstanding men advanced together, flourishing in cultivated accomplishment. The abundance of worthy men recruited rivaled the highest achievements of antiquity, leaving both Han and Tang behind.

Our reigning emperor has gloriously received Heaven’s favor and oversees the myriad affairs of government. He takes Heaven as his pattern and his ancestors as his models. His sagely learning is renewed daily; he orders ritual and harmonizes music, and his institutions are fully established. How brilliantly shines this era of renewed flourishing and cultural enlightenment! Scholars encountering…

title: 嘉靖三十一年應天府鄉試錄
text:
其盛負文武忠孝之懿者孰
不欲吐奇揚英攄用世之志
所謂聖作物睹千載一時此
其會也夫
留都根本重地
皇祖定鼎于兹山水奇勝光涵
聖化之渥培植非一日矣故元僚
碩輔代有顯聞後雋嗣興文
雅醞籍匡贊輔翊之効多所
弼成我
===
皇上紹
列聖之統
兹治兩京畿内諸士所謂產其
地而逢其時者其鼓舞興起
punctuated:
其盛，負文武忠孝之懿者，孰不欲吐奇揚英，攄用世之志？所謂聖作物睹，千載一時，此其會也夫！
留都根本重地，皇祖定鼎于兹，山水奇勝，光涵聖化之渥，培植非一日矣。故元僚碩輔，代有顯聞；後雋嗣興，文雅醞籍，匡贊輔翊之効，多所弼成。我皇上紹列聖之統，兹治兩京，畿内諸士，所謂產其地而逢其時者，其鼓舞興起
translation_en:
…amid this flourishing age, who among those endowed with the virtues of civil and military accomplishment, loyalty and filial devotion would not wish to display their exceptional talents and brilliance, and give expression to their ambition to serve the world? As the saying goes, “When the sage arises, all things behold him”: an opportunity occurring once in a thousand years. Surely this is that moment!
The auxiliary capital is a vital seat of the dynasty’s foundations. The imperial ancestor established his capital here; its mountains and waters are of extraordinary beauty, bathed in the abundant radiance of sagely transforming influence. Such cultivation has been the work of more than a single day. Thus eminent ministers and great counsellors have won renown in every generation. Talented successors have risen in turn, refined and cultivated in letters, and through their service in correcting, assisting, and supporting the throne have helped bring much to fruition. Our emperor has inherited the succession of the sage sovereigns and now governs the two capitals. The scholars within the metropolitan regions are precisely those described as born in the right place and encountering the right time; their inspiration and awakening…

title: 嘉靖三十一年應天府鄉試錄
text:
必先于四方矣嘗聞文章盛
衰與光岳之氣相應士之誦
習六經冲養和粹則心術光
明然後發之爲文足以表見
當世今肆閱諸士之文典而
雅者
===
制命之儲也雅而麗者聲歌之
則也婉而盡者詞文之軌也
簡而重者播告之宗也嚴而
辨者
諭詔之選也磨礱淹貫之質雄
渾敦大之氣皆于斯乎發之
譬則良冶之蓄型範莫同而
爲器則均
punctuated: 必先于四方矣。嘗聞文章盛衰，與光岳之氣相應。士之誦習六經，冲養和粹，則心術光明，然後發之爲文，足以表見當世。今肆閱諸士之文，典而雅者，制命之儲也；雅而麗者，聲歌之則也；婉而盡者，詞文之軌也；簡而重者，播告之宗也；嚴而辨者，諭詔之選也。磨礱淹貫之質，雄渾敦大之氣，皆于斯乎發之。譬則良冶之蓄，型範莫同，而爲器則均。
translation_en: …will surely precede those of all other regions. I have heard that the flourishing and decline of literary composition correspond to the vital energies of heaven and earth. When scholars recite and study the Six Classics, quietly nurturing harmony and purity, their minds and intentions become luminous; expressed in writing, these qualities then suffice to distinguish them in the present age. Now, upon broadly examining these scholars’ compositions, those that are canonical and refined provide a reserve for drafting imperial commands; those that are refined and splendid furnish standards for songs of praise; those that are subtle yet exhaustive offer models for literary expression; those that are concise and weighty provide exemplars for public proclamations; and those that are solemn and discriminating are choice material for imperial instructions and edicts. Their cultivated qualities and comprehensive learning, their vigorous, rounded, generous, and expansive spirit—all find expression here. They may be compared to the stock of a skilled metalcaster: though the molds differ, all alike become useful vessels.

title: 嘉靖三十一年應天府鄉試錄
text:
聖教誕被漸進斯不足徵矣乎諸
士藏器待用豈特緣飾辭章
規進取而已乎居激烈之懷
寧不欲追蹤伊傅周召與之
馳逐于百代之上耶得志之
後苟于富貴利達遂嘐然喪
其平生斯固不足以為士矣
===
是故
國家取士之制文也而用之則
行也名也而責之則實也實
循則行成行成則名茂而文
益顯是謂適用之才彼徒文
焉末已諸士誦法古人抗志
抱真必有先天下而出者行
punctuated:
聖教誕被，漸進斯不足徵矣乎？諸士藏器待用，豈特緣飾辭章、規進取而已乎？居激烈之懷，寧不欲追蹤伊傅周召，與之馳逐于百代之上耶？得志之後，苟于富貴利達，遂嘐然喪其平生，斯固不足以為士矣。

是故，國家取士之制，文也，而用之則行也；名也，而責之則實也。實循則行成，行成則名茂，而文益顯，是謂適用之才。彼徒文焉，末已。諸士誦法古人，抗志抱真，必有先天下而出者，行
translation_en:
The sage’s teaching spreads far and wide: is this not sufficient evidence of its gradually advancing influence? You gentlemen preserve your abilities and await employment; surely you do not merely embellish your compositions and seek advancement? Harboring such ardent aspirations, would you not wish to follow in the footsteps of Yi Yin, Fu Yue, the Duke of Zhou, and the Duke of Shao, and vie with them across a hundred generations? If, after attaining your ambitions, you settle for wealth, honor, profit, and advancement, and then, in boastful self-satisfaction [?], abandon your lifelong commitments, you are certainly unworthy of being called scholars.

Thus, the state’s system for selecting scholars rests on literary accomplishment, but their employment rests on conduct; selection rests on reputation, but what is demanded of them is substance. When substance is pursued, conduct becomes accomplished; when conduct becomes accomplished, reputation flourishes and literary accomplishment shines all the more. This is what is meant by talent suited to practical service. Those who possess literary accomplishment alone concern themselves merely with the peripheral [?]. You gentlemen recite the words of the ancients and take them as your models, elevate your aspirations, and hold fast to what is true. Among you there must be those who will emerge ahead of all others under Heaven. Soon …

title: 嘉靖三十一年應天府鄉試錄
text:
将進于春官揚之
大廷漸鴻振鷺効用四方其翕
張世道以宣風殿俗代工成
務當與古哲同垂耿光無亦
于爾始進乎占之故因卒事
致厚望焉
翰林院修撰汪鏜謹序
punctuated:
将進于春官，揚之大廷，漸鴻振鷺，効用四方。其翕張世道，以宣風殿俗，代工成務，當與古哲同垂耿光，無亦于爾始進乎占之？故因卒事，致厚望焉。
翰林院修撰汪鏜謹序。
translation_en:
…will soon advance to the Ministry of Rites and be brought to prominence at the great imperial court. Like wild geese ascending and egrets taking wing, you will render service throughout the realm. In shaping the course of the age, spreading civilizing influence, securing sound customs, and carrying out the work of government on the ruler’s behalf, you should leave a radiant legacy alongside the sages of antiquity. May we not foresee this even now, as you first advance? Thus, upon completing the examination, I express these high hopes for you.
Preface respectfully written by Wang Tang, Hanlin Academy Compiler.
